Ich bin wirklich überrascht von Warface!
Die verdammt gute Graffik, das aiming, die Atmusphere, alles!
Okay fangen wir mit der Graffik an:
Crytek an sich machen gute Spiele, die für die Graffiken und das Gamemod am meisten bekannt wurden.
Als ich das erste mal das Spiel spielte, wurde mir klar, wie verdammt gut die Atmusphere, die Graffik an sich und die texturen sehr realistisch gestaltet sind. Ich war auch beindruckt, wie viel megapixel es in sich reinstecken kann, damit der Spielspaß besser wird.
Jetzt zum Gamemod dieses Spiels:
Warface ist ein sogenanntes Online firstperson egoshooter mit Co-op modus und Herausforderung.
Das Spiel an sich beginnt erstmal mit einem Training, das dir alles zeigt, was dieses Spiel dir alles zum anbieten hat.
Du hast 4 verschiedene Klassen;
Söldner- sorgt für munition und ist stürmer
Mediziener- ist für Heilung und wiederbelebung zuständig
Engineur- Für panzerung und Sprengladungen gut gedacht
Scharfschütze- Schütze mit hoher präsizion.
Du kannst am anfang erstmal nur mit söldner oder Scharfschütze spielen, nach dem du paar Stufen hochgekommen bist, kannst du einen Training mit dem Medic starten. kommst du weiter hoch, kommt dann als nächster der Engineur.
Jede woche kommen neue Aufträge, wenn du co-op machen möchtest. Heißt also auch Normal-schwer-Wannsinnig.
Neue Spieler kriegen nur normal stufige Missionen. Damit das Spielen mit dem Schwierigkeiten ausgeglichen werden können.
Warface bietet nicht nur Co-op oder Herausforderungen, sondern auch noch TDM, Stürmen, Flagge erobern, DM, Kopfgeldjagt und noch mehr.
Damit das spielen nicht langweilig wird, kriegt man jedentag beim einloggen des spiels eine kleine "Wochenbelohnung".

Homefront: The Revolution is an ambitious FPS marred by its fraught development cycle. I was quite kind in a first-impressions review I did for this game, encouraging people to buy it for the insanely good sale price of £9, and whilst having played through and completed the game and its DLC ultimately leaves me with positive feelings on the whole, my recommendation is quite conditional.
H:TR is a semi-open world FPS about a silly alternate history in which North Korea invades the USA. NK led the digital tech boom in the 70s and dominated the US market with their technology. In the present day the US economy is failing and the country is globally disliked after numerous Middle Eastern wars, and after defaulting on a debt to NK they are invaded. The world is apparently okay with this, as it is performed under the facade of humanitarian aid, but NK's methods of control and suppression are brutal, and you begin the game finding yourself part of a revolutionary uprising to take back Philadelphia.
Your general goal is to liberate zones of KPA incursion, and you'll find yourself in one of two types of areas as the story progresses. Red zones are restricted to the public and the KPA will fire on sight, and can be cleared by conquering 'strike points' that free a small area of KPA troops and establish revolution forces. Your revolutionaries then dot the free zones, coming to your aid when you recruit them in an easy drop-in-drop-out system, and you feel powerful when you have a clutch of soldiers at your side, although once you figure out how to take a strike point out on your own, your fellow soldiers may become an afterthought. Once you’ve cleared the entire zone you move into a yellow zone - an inhabited area in which the KPA won’t shoot on sight, but set off an alarm and you’ll have to hide in order to escape their aggression. You’ll complete missions here whilst rallying the public behind you until they’re ready to revolt, after which you can begin liberating the zone as before. Attacking the strike points and freeing the zones is fun, but it is most of what you’ll be doing in the game. There’s a definite sense of repetition to the gameplay that may set in, however clever level design and nicely sculpted landscapes help to mitigate some of that feeling. The world appears meticulously designed, giving you a great freedom of movement and choice in tackling your objective.
It’s worth mentioning that the combat is a lot of fun. The way the KPA are designed to attack on sight in the red zones (but you can escape by fleeing or eliminating all witnesses), and be on guard the yellow zones (but any kind of open aggression will trigger an alarm that will bring incessant enemy troops), allows for lots of hit-and-run guerrilla-style attacks, and oftentimes you will start a fight confident only to have something tiny and unexpected go wrong and you find yourself fleeing for your life. The flow of combat feels very dynamic, and it rarely feels like a way to change the situation up, and although the checkpoint save system can be, at times, extremely frustrating, it doesn’t hurt to know that if you screw up and die, you’re going to be inconvenienced in terms of your real time, which gives the pitched battles a sense of immediate stakes.
However, when we talk about AI, or graphics, or story,  or any one of half a dozen topics, we come to a consistent theme permeating H:TR as a whole – a tug of war between elements that sell you and elements that expose the game as a daft and sometimes broken affair. The standalone base game is not something that I would recommend for full retail price as the much-documented AI problems and awkward silent protagonist are, sadly, the tip of the iceberg. There are many aspects of the game that are very buggy.
It’s worth keeping in mind before you buy that H:TR’s development process was fraught. The IP was passed around numerous publishing companies and development studios before completion. It was a mess, and caused massive problems for the developers both practically and mentally, as noted by the touching thank you message at the end of the credits. However, this doesn’t change the fact that my experience was marred start-to-finish by constant and imposing graphical glitches, specifically one in which a portion of the screen would turn a certain colour, usually black, which would then creep to obscure my entire view. You may not have these same issues – I noticed that even though my frame rate was solid on High settings, it was very taxing on my GPU, and others with better rigs might not have such troubles - but it’s still worth noting that you may notice some glaring technical issues in playing.
Had it been just the base game that I played (and I started writing this review before playing the DLC, after which I began a rewrite), I wouldn’t recommend H:TR without a massive discount simply for the pervasiveness of the technical problems I experienced. However, the DLC goes a long way to correcting the issues experienced and even redeeming the game. There are 3 DLC packs – Voice of the Revolution, a 1 hour long prologue in which you play as Walker (a somewhat central NPC in the main game) immediately before the events of the game; Aftermath, a couple of hours following the end of the main game in which you play as Ethan (now with a voice!) sent on a rescue mission; and Beyond The Walls, another couple of hours playing as Ethan, and the true finale of the game.
Content-wise, the DLC rights some of the wrongs in the base game. Ethan is a likable character when he’s allowed a personality. There’s one jibe about how he was better liked when he kept his mouth shut, but I found it easy to connect with him and start caring for him, even in the mere 3-4 hours you spend getting to hear him. The narrative is much more directed in the DLC, and combined with Ethan being voiced means that the DLC hits its emotional marks a lot better. VOTR is really short and carries a ‘Metro’ vibe as you battle raiders in the subways, and in terms of overall worth is neither here nor there. It’s nice to take a spin in the boots of a rather central main-game character, but it’s really quite short. Aftermath is a decent bit of fun, although again amounting to little more than a single mission. Its greatest achievement is in going some way towards establishing an emotional connection to two of the main characters that was all but lacking up until this point. BTW is the best bit of DLC in my opinion, and takes you out of the city into the sparsely patrolled countryside. There’s a pitched battle towards the end that really feels tense, the stakes feel high, and the ending left me genuinely emotional. The technical problems still appeared in the DLC, but being shorter and more directed, I didn’t feel the content was hindered quite as much by them. Because they are more linear, they allow for a greater motivation in your actions and the pacing is tightly controlled. Were the main game itself a greater combination of these directed sections with the open-world sections, perhaps there would have been a better sense of drama and less of a feeling of repetition.
After playing the DLC, my final opinion of H:TR as a whole changed wildly. Obviously, the developers had a hell of a time even getting it off the ground, and for all that is flawed about the main game, it can’t be said that it’s not highly ambitious in many important ways. But be aware that there are bugs, and while the bugs remain, I cannot recommend the main game alone for anything other than a heavy discount. Get it discounted with the DLC, however, (it cost me £9 all up in a great sale) and I’d call that a steal. I’d still not recommend it for the full price tag, but even if it were only £10 cheaper, I’d say that it’d still be worth it.

Многие считают Dark Souls 2 худшей в серии, и я понимаю их точку зрения. Но всё же считаю, что они неправы, и очень сильно занижают её достоинства и недостатки очень приукрашивают. Для того, чтобы вы поняли, о чём я, я хочу привести примеры недостатков остальных частей, которых нет у второй:
Dark Souls: блокировка на 30fps, отключённые сервера, посредственная система ПвП, просто ужасная оптимизация, и баланс (poise) сделан в упор на танков, что не позволяет нормально использовать лёгкое оружие. Есть просто ужасные боссы (Bed Of Chaos), нечестные моменты (Смерть на Нагом Сите), да и вообще у игры полно недостатков.
Dark Souls 3: Несмотря на запутанный левелдизайн, локации линейны и связь между ними идёт только на определённых перекрёстках, всё сводится к одному "хабу", из которого мы путешествуем, ПвП изначально было нацелено на спам лёгким оружием и до сих пор эффективны только 5-6 оружий из всех. Очень много заимствовано из предыдущих частей, оригинального контента меньше. Лор в некоторых местах не совпадает и запутывает. Ну и конечно то, что фантомы могут пить эстус. Также игра довольно коротка, что разочаровывает
Что же есть у Dark Souls 2?
Фантомы могут использовать лечение, но стоит кому-то вторгнуться, эта возможность им отключается. Левелдизайн во многих локациях вполне неплох, их интересно исследовать. То же расположение врагов в Shrine of Amana очень грамотное и поиск слепых зон-одна из ключевых тактик в этой локации. Poise здесь самый сбалансированный (простите за калабмур), можно играть как танком, так и лёгким воином. Арсенал оружия, эффективного в ПвП очень велик, и система прокачки оружия тут тоже самая понятная и эффективная. Из бесполезных зачарований могу назвать только Mundane, и то это после его нёрфа. У неё есть свой собственный лор, лишь слегка пересекающийся с первой частью. И Школяр Первого Греха отлично завершил лор. У неё также лучшие ДЛС среди трёх, по моему мнению, чего стоит только Элеум Лойс. Лучшая оптимизация, вполне неплохая графика и самая большая длительность прохождения, если брать прохождение со всеми DLC и со всеми боссами. Также введены особенности для New Game+, в то время как в остальных частях никаких изменений кроме урона и здоровья не было.
Подведём итоги: Dark Souls 2 плохая игра? Ни в коем случае. Хуже ли она остальных частей? Тоже нет. У неё есть свои недостатки, такие как однообразные боссы, система Soul Memory, слишком завышенное здоровье фантомов-NPC, но это всё! В остальном она на уровне первой и третьей, а иногда даже лучше. Если оценивать её, я поставлю ей твёрдые 8.5.

Verdun is a multiplayer squad based FPS set in World War 1.
You have specialised roles with differeing equipment available, but at the end fo the day, you're an easily punctured blood bag. You need to make good use of cover and squad tactics to survive as you make your way across the field. Once you are in the same area as the enemy, the fighting gets brutal and deadly. Close quarters combat in trenches and tunnels just accelerates the rate at which your fleshy blood bag dies and requires a respawn. Again, staying close to squadmates helps as they are basically mobile cover, unless someone throws a grenade, then you're all pretty much dead.
Aiming is mostly iron sights. Sharpshooters have scopes avaialble. If you manage to hit someone, you generally kill them.
My experience has been like this:
Spawn. Follow NCO around as he gives order to attack. Stop. Watch squadmate look over trench . Squadmate gets shot and falls dead. NCO charges over trench. Follow. NCO manages to get to cover. Run toward cover. Get shot. Die.
Respawn. Follow NCO. Stick to trenches. Round corner, get shot up by a squad of enemies. Die.
Respawn. Ditch NCO. Creep around trenches. Peek up over trench. Get shot. Die.
Respawn. Follow NCO. Get to attack point. Find cover. NCO and squadmates die. Hide. See enemy. Shoot. Miss. Cycle the bolt to reload. Enemy shoots. Misses. Shoot again. Kill enemy before he can shoot again. JOY! Get shot by his squadmate. Die.
Just as in history books, it goes back and forth, dying to take control of small section, and once your side has prevailed, you must defend it, and sometimes lose it and try to take it back again.
If you need to watch a show to get in the mood, watch Our Wolrd War. It was a series by the BBC.

Okay, so I've played long enough and I've made my mind up.
So, what do I think of the game? Well, I think it's a bloody mess.
Now you may be thinking "Why? Why is it a mess?"
Well it's a d@-mn good game, but it honestly is one of those games that really upsets me.
That you'll also ask "why" and that is because of the fact it's a decent game.
It's plauged by constant showcases of how NOT to do a paid system.
This game is basically filled with constant reminders of why this game is constantly called "pay to win".
For instance, when I was just starting out in PVP, I ran up unto a base that was literally armored with concrete walls, had RPG soldiers, LVL 10 MG Nests, and Level 8 sniper towers (possibly 8-9.) It's safe to say I was completely obliterated.
This being only JUST AFTER I was out of the tutorial, and unto my first few base assaults.
So, I did a test. For a single day I was going to play the game entirely without paying a cent.
The results? Absolutely F#$^ ing horrid. The game was practically un-enjoyable, I was constantly being killed, and sometimes even being outgunned by the same type of soldiers, just decked out with perk upgrades. Not to mention when I kept running into high-level defences, I kept dying, and dying, and dying. Don't get me wrong, I still progressed, but the soldiers I had were so under-upgraded, that every conflict I engaged in usually resulted in them STOMPING my troops, and blitzkreiging all the way up to my command car, and blowing it up.
The next day I did another test: Pay cash, see the end result. I paid only 5 Dollars.
After I paid, I proceeded to use the gold to buy a "new recruit pack" which basically gave me all the sh-it I needed to see this was CLEARLY pay-to-win. (Others might say otherwise, but I've seen it first-hand. The game is UNBALANCED and needs clear balancing.) Now you may say "what did you get that makes you think this?" Well, I got perks that basically made my soldiers into super soldiers. (Only being defeated by other p2w'ers.) Plus, I got a legendary HQ defence squad.
(Minigun, RPG, and the other rifles, plus one medic.) Any time someone came to the base in retaliation, they basically got decimated by the HQ squad, only one person managed to win, and that person basically had almost every bloody unit, plus a large sum of attack cards. (Yea... balancing fixes needed.)
Now, I need to also point out, technically you can obtain most of this stuff "FREELY" by opening crates, but there's a big issue: KEYS DO NOT DROP OFTEN ENOUGH TO EVEN JUSTIFY OPENING THEM. I have only gotten the amount to open ONE CRATE ONLY, and that was after basically TWO DAYS of playing. Guess what's gonna open it faster? GOLD. Seriously, it's basically a chokehold of "You either pay, or get stuck at a SEVERE disadvantage."
Overall, I really wish I could say "download this game". I mean, even with all the bad examples, I REALLY enjoy the game. But there is far too many P2W aspects for me to even justify it, plus too many people trying to paint a picture that it's "Not pay to win, just pay to progress faster". It is not progression you pay for, you can pay for better units, you can pay for better upgrades for units. Plus, you can also pay to get card bundles which can give you more munitions, AND more upgrades.
tl;dr version:
decent game, needs to have keys drop more frequently. (this does not mean lessen the amount of loot you get in exchange for faster drop. Keep the loot the same, make the keys drop faster.) Balance the matchmaking, and try to make the game less P2W. That's all.

Homefront: The revolution is the first homefront game I have experienced, missing out on the first one. This being my first game of the series I had a wide range of expectations and came into the game only knowing it was powered by the far cry 3 engine.
Story:
So far I have mainly played through the main storyline, looting on the side to keep my self content with resources i had for the easy crafting system. The main storyline is fairly easy to follow and due to decent immersion and storytelling you can take the role of your character very easily. The characters are well thought out and introduced well.
7/10
Graphics:
Due to having a over-all lower spec PC (i5-4460, GTX750TI, 8GB of RAM and no SSD) I had low expectations when it came to running a game such as this, I run it on primarily medium settings and only have experienced any kind of noticable frame drops when in a gameplay location where there is lots of dust. Apart from that it looks very visually appealing, and when I have ran it on higher settings the game does look very nice, good lighting and very immersive matching the game.
8/10
Gunplay:
Knowing this was powered with the far cry engine I thought the combat would feel very out of place for such a action packed game and playing far cry, know it feels out of place. However I with a lot of guns it really does suit the futuristic vigilante aesthetic and whilst the guns dont feel TOO floaty they don't feel like they should pack the boom they really do. The guns are fairly balanced and all have a very nice range of options when it comes to attachments/customisation. With each primary gun in the game having two split options to modify it, then along with options (in most cases) for a Barrel customisation, Under Rail customisation and Scope customisation. Having 3 gun slots gives you the options to change your playstyle quickly and to very varied playstyles. I have found combining these to be the most efficient way to play.
7/10
UI:
The UI is quick to understand, well designed and pleasing to use. It gives you the relevant information you need without feeling cluttered or covering too much of your screen. The mini-map is pretty useful, showing you a lot of information meaning you have a lot to do, as anything you pass you can view on the minimap. This gives you a nice advantage during fights as you can see enemy drones, targets, soldiers, heavies ETC.
9/10
AI:
The AI is about standard for any game like this. I've had some moments in the games stuck due to NPC's, or NPC's getting stuck when following me ATC but none of these have been a real issue, just walking away and back fixes it most times. It appears if a NPC is following you and gets stuck they teleport when you get far enough away anyway. This game makes the friendly AI you have actually seem balanced, they call out special units, actually do damage, dont die right away, stick with you well and provide more cover for you obviously.
8/10
Optimisation:
Well, considering my specs mentioned earlier the game is optimised very well, honestly i'm surprised with how well it runs on my rig, managing to stay above 45FPS whilst I have a browser open with a youtube video playing whilst I play the game.
8/10
Pros:
Honestly a fun to play game - sets the world very well, fairly immersive experience. Worth a try if you just come into the game with no expectations from prior games or hype built aroud before release.
Cons:
There are honestly bugs, the same as all games, I've experienced 2 noticable ones from 7 hours of gameplay over three sessions.
Worth pickining up?
If you pick it up whilst its on sale at 75% then yes, £7.99 is a fair price for this game. I would not pay the full retail price (on steam) and say you wait for a sale.

So far so good, enjoying the new setting and the open feel of the world with the outdoor textures, the game has crashed once after about an hour, going to try fiddling with the settings until an update clears that up.
I will update the review as I play
MODES +
-OLD SCHOOL for the added punishment of having to hand draw your map on paper
-IRON MAN means you can only save at blue crystals
-SINGLE USE CRYSTALS for my fellow masochists
-OLD SCHOOL IRON MAN SINGLE USE CRYSTALS for people who thought Dark Souls was far too easy and wish they could find something with a little more challenge
SURVIVAL +
-Injury mechanic now means you can lose use of an arm, legs, regeneration of health and energy, can be cured with Blue crystals and I imagine there will be a potion i have yet to discover as well
-Food and Potion ingredients can now be farmed with the new farmer and alchemist class allowing for extended gameplay and new playstyles

WORLD +
-The new world is primarily on the island of Grimrock instead of the interior of the mountain in the previous installment. The textures are a little under par for games these days but for 800MB download it's pretty good. within the first hour you'll experience a beach, a crypt and a forest, just to show the diversity of area's on offer so far.
CHARACTERS ++
-Characters have been overhauled and so far i can't complain, more classes and an extra race open up the party formation and can take a lot of thought depending on your play style,
-The new ratling race is more for storage and less combat focused
-Alchemist class grows plants for potions and uses firarms
-Battle mage class is a combination of a mage and a fighter
-Farmer class for food, not much else...
-Fighter class weapon skill focus
-Berserker class health and damage focus
-Knight class health and armour focus
-Rogue class for throwing, dual wielding and bows/crossbows
LEVELLING +
-Stat points are now automatic and depend on your class, I don't mind this as it simplifies the process without taking anything away from the game
-Stats can be improved by having a healthy diet specific to the race of character
-Skills are now all open to every class and have 5 tiers with ability unlocks at certain tiers, for example accuracy skill tier 2 allows for attacking with melee from the back row
EXPLORATION +
-Can feel a little different at first with the new setting but just start wandering and remember to check every wall and every square of the map
-Underwater and you can catch fishy's, though they are our friends, not food (you can eat them)
COMBAT ++
-Melee feels a little slowed down, be it very fractional, less spammy, more impact, makes kiting a little more difficult, still just as fun (might just be my impression as it is very subtle)
-Ranged seems to have been expanded with the addition of guns and bullets as well as what seems like a larger variety of weapons.
-Spell system has been overhauled, you no longer click a combination of the 3x3 spell panel, but draw a line in one motion, I imagine this would be more for touch based devices but it works fine and streamlines the job of casting.
MONSTERS ++ (X2 Pirate bonus)
-Feels balanced for early levels, not to hard to beat, not a cake walk.
-Yet to find a monster being reused from Grimrock 1
-First Boss was quite fun
-Pirate theme, pirate rats
MAP EDITOR
-Yet to try, but can't wait with all the new features in game alone it should be a blast

The legend of Grimrock had given a second life to the first person tile-based dungeon crawlers. The legend of Grimrock II has done it again for me. The game already feels "bigger" as you explore, not just a dungeon like in the previous one, but the island of Nex, which is filled with a multitude of dungeons.
If you liked the first game, you will definetely love this one! I clearly recommand this game, which puts even more place to the "exploration" part with outside areas, and more dungeons, as well as a lot of secrets to find.
In term of content, the game already puts the bar higher than its predecessor, giving old items from grimrock, but also a lot of brand new items, which would probably remind of old school games from the 80's-90's, like notably a wodden staff, or also a sling. There are brand new monsters, as well as some from the previous game (According to the website, 44 monsters with 12 from the previous game), and the game feels fresh due to this.
Also, the biggest change in the game is its beauty, as you travel outside, you get to see some marvelous areas, which is better than the 3 area types we see in mount grimrock.
In term of gameplay and difficulty, the game proposes 7 classes and 5 races (1 being new), which is more than its predecessor. The skill system is different though, proposing less perk levels (5 for each) but only 1 skill point per level. Also there is now a "local damage" system, which can prevent you from using a weapon slot, or make you slower, prevent your health or energy to come back up, ect, ect... And most notably for the adventurers who want the hardest challenges, they can set life crystals to be usable only once, and/ or to be the only way to save the game.
In any case, I would say this game simply blows, and, being much more complete than its predecessor, should have an even longer life thanks to the dungeon editor, and the creativity of the community.

So I've got a couple of hours into the game so far, and I wanted to share my thoughts, since I was a bit skeptical at first as well.
Short review:
Pros:
- Great outdoor scenery, complete with water that you can wade into, as well as natural terrain that can be walked on.
- Underwater swimming with enemies, hidden items, and drowning.
- Greatly expanded character customization, tons more possibilites than original game.
- Some enemies start to retreat when on low health, and you have to chase them to finish them off.
- Enemies prove to be a challenge and take advantage of your mistakes, includes counter-attacks for creating distance and the strafe-n-hit tactic that made the first Grimrock easy.
- Many, many new enemies, probably at least triple the amount of last game.
- Boss fights! The first one is not too challenging, but then again it is the first boss :3
- Spellcasting improvements; spellcasting can be drawn out instantly or premade like in the first game, and it also shows you what you're casting before you click cast if you've used the spell once before.
- Guns! Yeah, seriously, there's guns. Ammo for guns cannot be retrieved, but it comes in larger amounts and does more damage.
- Some area transitions involve horizontal movement instead of vertical, staircase movement (although stairs are still present).
- The map is connected in a large grid, making it easy to see where certain levels connect.
Neutral:
- Limbs can be damaged and unusuable until healing
Cons:
- The game is harder to run, I notice a performance drop specifically when saving. Otherwise it's still very playable.
I will update this list as I see more things worth noting :)
More in-depth review:
Before even being an hour into the game, I quickly realized how much further Legend of Grimrock could be taken mechanic-wise. Every single addition to the game that I've seen has not only improved, but expanded on the original core game. Mechanics like swimming, new logic, outdoor enviornments, and full buildings are only a few of the new additions that I've seen in my brief time in Nex.
If you were disappointed with the original combat system with its exploitable strafe-n-hit tactic, then I'm sure you'll be happy to know that most enemies have trained for that. I have a lot of practice with the tactic, and using it in the sequel so far has led to a lot of quick, hard hits from enemies. From quick diagonal strikes from skeletons to jump attacks from imps to evasive rolling from walking trees (treants?), you're going to get smacked before you fully move into the tile to attack.
If you enjoyed the original game, buying this should be an easy choice. It's another incredible adventure with more to come from the workshop.

Summary: Great game, bad port. Also, do not buy if you rely on Lulu's overdrive.
This is a review for Final Fantasy X's HD remaster. I have not tested the other games yet.
VERY mixed reception from me on this one. On the one hand, it's a great game. On the other hand, the port has TONS of technical problems. I'm giving this a "No" for recommendation to raise awareness and because there are still fully-functioning console versions.
For one, it crashes like crazy when playing on settings above what your PC can handle-- which might be expected, but the problem is that that description is completely unknowable and extremely finicky. No slowdown, just staight-up crashing unexpectedly over and over. It's infuriating and ridiculous. Expect to angrily mess around a lot with graphics settings to find the highest ones you can play it on without crashes and freezing-- but you may have to play for 30 minutes before the random crash happens.
Also, the button mapping is less than stellar. Instead of just allowing you to remap what used to be the PS2/PS3/PS4 controls, the PC port controls does its own thing and everything's really confusing. Also, no soft reset. That's ridiculous with a game full of Square-Enix-Hard minigames.
What's even worse, Auron's overdrive is extremely difficult to do compared to the console versions, and Lulu's overdrive is confirmed broken. You get less than half the spell casts for the same amount of hard work-- and yes, we did check verify Lulu's stats and use the right controls. It is BROKEN. Say goodbye to Lulu-only challenges on this port.
The built-in cheats are so minimal I don't even know why they bothered. An instant max overdrive success cheat is much-needed, by the way. And finally, you can only skip a few cutscenes. Most of them are unskippable-- and yes, there ARE too many unskippable FMVs.
Things are messy all around. I absolutely DEMAND a fix for Lulu's overdrive. Don't even argue with me if you haven't tried using it, because her overdrive will do LESS damage than a normal spell cast! It is completely broken and this is unacceptable.

One of my personal favorite JRPGs of all time, full of great characters and an interesting world to explore.
All characters in the main cast have a role to play both in the story and in combat, thanks to the Sphere Grid system. This allows a decent degree of customization when leveling up the party, although there is a clear niche for each character to fill. These niches extend to the characters Overdrives (similar to Limit Breaks in other FF games), and each character has a different gimmick ranging from quick-time events to slot machines to combining items.
The story premise is interesting, incorporating many classic Final Fantasy elements. There are many emotional highs and lows throughout.
The visual design and soundtrack do a great job of aiding the worldbuilding, making each character and location both feel and sound unique.
Battles are fully turn-based, although there are many ways to alter the turn-order, and the active party members can be switched in and out on the fly. The difficulty curve is fairly well-balanced, although there are a couple bosses in the story that are very difficult and require some grinding or very clever strategies.

Kind of intriguing. A twist on the usual strategy game elements. base building is no longer recquired, and you have a selection of "hero" units at your disposal that can call in reinforcements. Basic units such as rangers or medics, even tanks and humvees, can level up and become "promoted" to a hero unit. Each hero unit has specific abilities based around their original class. For instance, the marksman(sniper) unit can upgrade into a veteran Sniper, giving him abilities like stealth, and the ability to recquisition units like scout helicopters and humvees. As said, it's intriguing and worth a look. There is a demo in the steam store, and if not, you can download the demo from
. Trust me, even though the voice acting is a little iffy at times, you can't judge based on cutscenes and chatter. it's the gameplay that counts and thats what this game has.

I wasn't expecting to enjoy this as much as I have.  I thought at best, it'd be a fun little game to spend a few hours in.  I've put in more consecutive time here than I have Fallout 4.  At the time of writing this, I am still not burned out on it.
:
+Graphics are mostly terrific.  Some Superstars/Divas are spot on.  Others don't seem to have had as much attention to detail put into them (not that they're ugly, just that they aren't as good as the really good ones).
+Create modes. Holy isht, create modes.  Create Superstars, Divas, Entrances, Arenas, Shows, Titles... the CAW was always the draw to these games, and it has been greatly expanded upon here.  Face uploads make for creating anyone you can imagine without much effort, and with logo/texture uploads, you're really only limited by your imagination.
+Sharing these creations is so easy now.  If you've used the Community Creations of The Sims 4, you'll feel right at home here.  Anything you create (even move-sets) can be uploaded and easily downloaded.  WWF CAW vets will appreciate this - no more writing down CAW parts!  Just share that sucker!
+Match types.  Plenty of must-have matches have made a return.  TLC, Elimination Chamber, Hell in a Cell, Steel Cage, Royal Rumble, Last Man Standing, Submission, Battle Royal.  That's not to say they're perfect, which I'll get into in the Con's.
+The Roster.  Largest roster to date in any WWE game, and arguably the best.  It reaches back into WWE history and presents dozens of favorites and familiars.  Some of these even have alternate attires or versions.  Add CAW's to the list, and you're looking at 200+ fighters.
+Mechanics.  I spent time playing No Mercy and Day of Reckoning waiting for this release, and I wasn't sure how I'd feel about the leap from arcade to simulation.  It's not as bad as people say it is, and I usually hate QTE-type things, but I find them enjoyable here.  It's nice to have control over how you place and evade grapples/holds, and I feel missing the kick out of a pin because of poor timing adds to that "Oh, come on WWE, how could that happen?" feel you get watching the actual program sometimes.  And like No Mercy, the grapple system is multi-layered.  If you've played No Mercy, you know what I'm talking about.  It literally feels like they mashed No Mercy, Day of Reckoning, and Here Comes the Pain into one big, beautiful baby.
+Customization.  This is the best part of the game.  In Universe mode, you can control who's in what show, who they face, and who their rivals are.  It's like a very hands-on Exhibition mode.  Outside of Universe, you can control how the game plays by toning down (or pumping up) the new simulation systems.  You can control what music plays in the main menu.  You can even tweak the individual Superstar/Diva stats, both in Exhibition and in Universe.

:
-Some matches are not included as team sets.  For instance, I haven't seen any tag team TLC's.  Such a shame, as tag-team TLC was usually among me and mine's favorite match types.  It's a bit odd see it in singles, but not to see the beloved team version.

-Royal Rumble is gender-restricted.  2K16 does not feature a Diva Royal Rumble.  Surely there are enough Divas in the vanilla version to do a 10-woman rumble, but adding CAD's to it, and I see no reason the women couldn't have one.  At least they can do the other matches.
-No mixed matches.  I get it, I understand it, there is nothing that can be said I haven't seen/heard on the issue.  I do not want to be a man hitting a woman.  I want to be a woman hitting a man.  Specifically, Stephanie McMahon.   Beating Brock Lesner.  What's your problem?  The point of WWE video games is to create (or re-create) your dream matches with your favorite WWE characters, and Stephanie McMahon happens to be my favorite.  I can set males to be her enemies, but nothing ever comes of it.  We have Super Mario CAW's fighting Freddy Krueger CAW's.  It's not practical, it's not probable, it certainly isn't representative of WWE, but damn, is it enjoyable.  That's what made the classic games so great - you could have your serious recreations, or you could have totally insane stuff... or, you could be like me, and just want to have your favorite/created Diva be the face of your WWE game.  To ignore mixed matches does very little to protect women... in fact, it makes them appear more fragile.  Not including mixed matches as a possiblity speaks to the WWE's confidence in their current Diva's - both that their personalities are not strong enough to clash with their male counterparts in a digital space, and that their fanbase isn't large enough to want to do so.  Add to the fact that I have to hear Jerry "The King" Lawler spew his sexist comments during a Diva's match ("I may be too old for her, but she certainly isn't too young for me...") as a ring-side announcer, and I roll my eyes at the "respect women" excuse for no mixed matches.  I hate to make this such a political statement when I'm not really seeking equality on a grand scale, just a better game.  Ah, well, hopefully mods will fix this.
-Universe can be redundant.  I'm okay with this, but I list it for those that may be curious.  I figure, Exhibition will be redundant eventually.  At least with Universe, there's a chance of seeing some good random match-ups.
-Lack of notable faces.  No Charlotte Flair, no Dudley Boyz, no Sasha Banks, no Alberto Del Rio (so, no official League of Nations team).  Easily remedied through creation mode, but the over abundance of Triple H's and Undertakers makes you kinda wish these stars were included instead.
-Undertaker from his Fred Durst years is the strongest 'Taker without tweaking him yourself.
All in all, this is a terrific game, and you can make any Superstar/Diva you want the center of your Universe, albeit with a few warts.  It's been a good minute since I've felt this freedom in a WWE game (pre-SvR and DoR titles), and I've never felt it to the extent I have in 2K16.  Couple this with the gameplay, and I can see myself playing this for years to come... unless 2K17 greatly expands on it (fingers crossed... 2K15->2K16 was a considerable leap).

A 2 hour long interactive picture book if you look for EVERYTHING that lasts about an hour at most (maybe longer if you don't read well, actually sit through all the sloooowly spoken dialogue, or have trouble finding stuff, I spent a LOT of time looking for things that just weren't there trying to prove to myself that I didn't waste my money).  That's the best way to describe this.  Would have made an ok short story, but as a game it's just dull.  Pick a thing up, read something or someone talks to you, move to the next thing.
This tends to be my view of all walking sims, they're picture books you interact with, and honestly I'd rather just read it if there's no meat to it.  No real puzzles, no challenges and most importantly no failure state means I just can't support this being called a game.   And YES there could have been plenty of little challenges to make it a "game".  This is the story, from what I remember, of a teenager, they couldn't have owned a puzzle box or two to hold their things?  Couldn't have had some diary entries or notes written in code?  Couldn't have had a story item hidden and put 2-3 clues for a neat scavenger hunt?  Yes I did these things as a teenager, and yes it was fun.  You can have walking sims (which are interactive books, not games) and add content that will make it into a game.  It's not hard if you try.
Now I love me the hell out of narrative, story is the most important thing in a game to me, but when the story wouldn't even be 20 pages if it were in a book, then why am I paying so much for it in "game" form?  If this were 2-3 bucks I'd probably say to give it a try if you like this sort of thing, but for 20 damn bucks?  No, not on your life.  When you can watch the game on youtube and get the EXACT SAME experience as playing it yourself, then: 1 it's not a game and 2 the dev failed to even try to make it one.
TL;DR:  An interactive pop up book basically that's not terrible like some people say, however charging 20 bucks for this "game" is a sure fire sign that the devs are too damn full of themselves.  5 bucks MIGHT be ok for this but not 20 bucks.  There are hundreds of much MUCH better games out there with stories as good or better than this that feature actual game play.  And for a lot of them you can get 5 or 6 of those games for the same price.

I started out thinking "Well, I'll just relax with this restaurant managment game" and before I realized what was going on i was dating some short woman with a potato fetish and had become a media darling due to my participation in a series of televised  cooking competition while some guy tried to sell me his slightly used latex gloves.
No but really. This game is a really good one, well worth the money and kept me entertained for hours upon hours.
Pros:
- A nice balance between stressful and skill based (the skill you will learny quickly, everything will run much smoother once you've become familiar enough with the dishes to know which button to press for which ingredient and so on.
- Charming graphics and animations.
- A certain sense of accomplishment is always allowed but not forced upon the player, hence players who prefer calmer playthrough can choose to not drown themselves in repetable tasks that really don't get you that much in the game anyhow while players who need encouragement to sustain their interest can work towards the daily challenges available to you.
- A nice increasing curve of challenge which allows the player ot become accostumed to the frantic stress of their expanded restaurant before there's a new upgrade.
- You get to build your own restaurant freely and the menu of the restaurant freely as there are so many dishes available and you have to purchase most of them to make them available to you, then upgrade them.
- A certain feeling of the game being realistic as a result of the mechanism around buzz and daily popularity.
Cons:
- The sounds of the game become really annoying over time, the mumbling of the customers in particular.
- The buttons stuck a few times for me when i tabbed out or opened the steam overlay and I had to reboot the game.
- Although I quite enjoyed the fact that you were forced to get accustomed to each star to your restaurant and the customers that come with in the beginning, 20 days seemed excessive at the end as I was mostly just wanting to finish the game when I'd finished all extra material and has 15 days left for my restaurant to gain its last star. At that point i just forced myself through the gameplay, which is never a good thing.
Conclusion:
A good game indeed. Well worth the purchase.
For people who may be thinking of getting this game: don't rush doing your challenges, you have lots of time. And keep dedicated to your dating life in the game, your partners will all break up with your eventually (my heart is at this point as dark and bitter as my soul) but they will give you nice prizes upon doing so.

I thought that Cook, Serve, Delicious (CSD) was one of the best hidden gems available on Steam when I first found it. Now that this new and FREE expansion pack has come out, I also think that it's one of the best deals on Steam.
Cook, Serve, Delicious features a very simple style of game play: basically, it's all about having sharp reflexes and knowing you home row keys. Orders come up, and then you, as a cook, follow the simple commands to cook each order. But before you know it, your fingers are flying across the keyboard serving up orders with ridiculous speed!
This style of game play could easily become repetitive before long, but your recipes, and thus your button commands, are always changing, keeping the game play fresh. Newer recipes are added to old ones and are often more difficult and complex, consequently constantly increasing the difficulty of the game even as the player becomes more familiar with recipe commands.
Outside of the core game play (the back end of the restaurant, if you will) the options are also very solid. There are plenty of goals to meet, new foods and impactful upgrades to purchase, and a number of challenges to accept outside of the core game mode to keep things interesting. And on top of it all, the game is oozing with originality and humor. The art style is fun and unique and complements the game play quite well.
This newest expansion pack adds a number of new game play modes, but it will take some experience with the standard game modes before newcomers will be ready for these tough new challenges. The addition of leader boards, coop modes, and weekly challenges are all welcome additions as well.
I personally do not have any major issues with the game. It's well thought out, highly original, and has plenty of content for its price tag. It's a game that I think is totally deserving of its $10 and is game that I would recommend that absolutely anyone give a try.

"CSD" is a fun, relatively light game that combines keyboard skills (at least, if you choose to use the keyboard, though I think that's optimal), a little bit of memory, task prioritization and multi-tasking. If that's all you need to know, you'll enjoy it.
A "hardcore restaurant sim"? Heh, no... Not quite. No surly wait staff swiping each others' tips, no customers getting angry despite getting their orders right because they said one thing and meant another, no equipment breakdowns or grease fires. You *will*, however, have to flush the toilet half a dozen times a day, bait rat traps within a tight time window, receive money from celebrity chefs for serving customers without a mistake, and make three hundred dollar bets with a random anonymous stranger over e-mail.
You buy new foods and then never pay for them again, unless you choose to upgrade them. The most challenging part of making a pizza is remembering that olives are tied to the "V" key and onions to the "N". And your customers will grouse if you give them a jumbo water with ice instead of a large water with ice (though they'll still pay soda prices for water... apparently the Tower has no drinking fountains.)
None of this is suggesting changes to the game (I'd just as soon run a restaurant in the game's largely happy and straightforward world!), but if you're expecting a hardcore restaurant simulation, you might be a bit disappointed. If I did have to lodge one complaint, it would be that one has to do twenty "days" of service in order for one's restaurant to gain a "star", even if one's customer service is consistently perfect. This seems to have far less to do with anything believable within the game's "world" than with not wanting players to trundle through the amount of content the game provides too quickly. I understand that, but I don't have to applaud it.
What "CSD" offers is a colorful, fun, easy to grasp game that you can play for twenty minutes and walk away feeling you've done well. In that niche, it performs admirably.

Absolutely great game! This is not a mindless shooter per se, it's a dexterity based shooter where you need to use your intellect in order to pass some levels. It's not about just shooting every enemy in the stage, sometimes you just need to destry targets and proceed to the next level.

Game is full of weird humor but it's fun actually. In what other game you need to shoot hamburgers summoning boars or giraffes in a ufo shaped vehicles?
One guy wrote that there is not enough ammo in this game. Sometimes yes, but in most cases you can end up with maximum of 99 bullets every other stage. Just wait a moment untill morse stall produces ammo. Have in mind that you don't need to destroy all enemies most of the times.
Useful spoilerfree hints:
- if you score enough points in arcade machine minigame the machine explodes and you can collect a rocket
- you can click ENTER at the big red button limited amount of times - untill it explodes actually. Just click both enters - standard return enter and num lock enter if you have it to speed up the process.
- when those things explode, arcade machine and big red button, they can hurt you. Just be sure to stand as far as to highlight the Enter or E button to use those, but don't stand too close or you can get hurt
- if you feel that the level is too hard and happen to have 100 ducks then you can build the last building for 100 ducks to skip that level. Just wait a moment and the usual elevator appears.
- at some levels you can be cursed with flying yellow thingies on blue balls all around character. This can happen if you go too close to the blue totem thing. Worry not, if there is a fireplace you can position yourself so the fire hurts those flyers and eventually destroys them.
Pros:
- humor
- graphics are nice
- toxic themed stages are really fun and well designed
- music is pleasant to listen and well composed for this game
Cons:
- some levels are really hard. That's not a problem, but if you lose you need to start whole level all over again.
- at every level you start zoomed. You can of course zoom out but what't the problem with the auto zoom at every level? Really, with the perspective zoomed in you can barely see anything happening.
- it's too short:) I have like 7 hours on the counter but I feel that you can beat this game in about 4-5 hours as there are only 10 areas/levels with like 5-6 maps each. No secret levels or anything like that sadly.
In summary - I really recommend this game. Such fine a piece of an indie game.

Dungeon crawling in the style of Eye of the Beholder at its modern finest.  A fantastic sequel to the first legend of Grimrock.  Almost everything from the original returns, and almost everything has been improved upon.
The developers have spared no effort to improve upon the foundation set in the first game.  Let's start with building a party.  There is significantly more depth this time around.  This new game has 8 classes up from the original 3, 5 races up from the original 4.  But it doesn't end there.  Tool tips provide more information.  Classes no longer lock you to a set of 6 specific skills.  Rather, there are 16 total skills that you are able to choose between to customize your character how you see fit.  You want a frontline knight who also can cast a poison bolt here or there?  Done.  The number of options also leads to a large number of interesting choices.  Sure, an insectoid has great mental stats making for a natural wizard.  But they can also get superior armor, making them easily able to play the tankiest of tanks.
All these options will warm the hearts of anyone that loves to get deep into the numbers.  While I find building a party great fun, don't worry if that is not your cup of tea.  The game provides a default party that you can use, and it doesn't take a lot of work to make a barbarian that focuses in strength, damage, and more strength.
As an aside, the character portraits have gotten a major and much needed overhaul.  Your party will look much better than last time around, guaranteed.
Once you have a party you are dumped on an island.  Filled with common pirate tropes the designers do a good job of pulling you in, with a steady stream of monsters, loot and puzzles that all gradually increase in strength.  The monsters are a major improvement over Grimrock 1.  There is a greater variety right out of the gate.  In addition this game has added memorable boss encounters, something the first game in the series lacked.  The environments too are more varied, adding above ground areas to the strictly dungeoneering of the first game.  And the maps are much larger.
There are new options and attention to detail everywhere.  There are now day and night cycles.  You can dig for treasure.  Combat now includes firearms and dual wielding.  New kinds of puzzles.  Larger variety of weapons and improved weapon descriptions.  Tons of new loot.  You will need all of your new toys to succeed, because like the first one combat can be tough for the unprepared.
Top to bottom this game is an improvement over the original.  This is a modern take on classic dungeon crawling that is very satisfying for fans of the genre.

After having played every single F1 game except last years I was hoping for some larger changes to the game itself as it had started to become really stale and this year's version of F1 has delivered on improving upon that. F1 2016 is returning to the game I hoped F1 would become over time and it's virtually every thing I wanted, but falls a little short in a few areas.
One of the things I wished would change is the career. It had become stale, generic...no podium. It didn't feel engaging. This year improves upon that. It's nice to see your driver have a face and there is a nice clip of a podium etc if you get in the top 3. You soon get sick of these clips though and the novelty wears off.
It's kind of the same thing with your R&D rep, who every single time after you complete an upgrade has to come tell you that you have an upgrade. Again, it gets grating. They could of gave him some different animations or different lines and instead he just ends up getting on your♥♥♥♥♥♥ I can also say that about your agent, (I quite like the rival system btw). Who drops a rival on you every now and then, her dialogue becomes boring and old. Starts to rub on you.
This stuff is there to try and engage you more and for the first few races it does. After that, it doesn't count for much. So I wish that side of things, was more engaging and kept you engaged. I like the direction its going, just not quite there.
The driving, is superb. Now I'm using a controller. I know there have been some complaints about using one. I havent run into any issues at all. It's been great to control, feels good and not too twitchy. Haven't tweaked any settings it just ran fine. All tracks are really well recreated and another improvement from previous games is that you can use some of the kerbs instead of them feeling like they are made of ice.
Tyre wear feels better than previous versions. They seem to have nailed the feeling of losing grip and responsiveness of your tyres and when they start to go, you're losing time.
The A.I feels competitive too, after patches they have got even better arguably. They fight for positions and if the difficulty meter works well for your own ability, then it makes for some great races. I know that some people have mentioned that the levels up are too tough, to be honest, I'm racing on a level that is perfect for me. Haven't really had this issue. The added safety car adds more depth as well as the mostly pointless formation lap. It's good that it's there though.
Performance of the game is a little hit and miss. Patches for me have made the game perform slightly worse in certain areas and better in others. I am using an i5 4690 and GTX 1070 everything is on max and it runs between 60- 80 FPS occasionally CPU usage will spike for no real reason in some inexplicable areas. Like in the pits OR when I am waiting to access the laptop. Just random CPU spikes. Even with Vsync. So it could do with some work optimisation wise I think.
On the whole though, I've really enjoyed the time I've spent in single player with this game and I'm certain I'll be spending a lot more. It looks good, plays quite smoothly, drives well, AI is good and theres not a silly amount of bugs.

First time I heard about this game was when my (then) favorite streamer played an early version of the game, it looked nice and seemed like a cool game. Recently it was on sale and I thought "Finally, my time to play it!". Now, a couple of hours later, I'm mostly glad I did. Mostly? Yes, that's right.
If we were to take it all step by step, the game to me is great looking, the sound is creating some great atmosphere and immersion, the gameplay is for the most part rather simple - one part driving a train and making sure your passengers stay alive until their final destination, one part looting, shooting "zombies" and... staying alive yourself. So far, so good, right?
Then comes the story. From what I could gather, there had been some kind of Alien invasion a "while" back and now they're back and every human being has been infected by some "virus", turning them into monsters. You're playing as a nameless guy, conducting a train. Your train is the only train left running on the tracks. Why? Can't tell you. It's kind of sad that the story telling is lack luster as I'd love to know more about what was going on.
In the end, I was left wanting more of what I just spent some hours on. I know there's DLC, but I don't know... maybe some kind of sequel? I mean, they can't be the only ones on the planet. However, I really do recommend it - for full price or on sale, it doesn't matter.

This game has potential. SOOOO much potential.
First the things I like:
-Mechs
-Great customization
-Good unit variety
-Research
-base building
-novel level ideas, such as the stealth mission
-Well written (IMO) campaign
Unfortunately, while this game does some things very well, it has a number of what I consider to be major issues:
-Your unit AI is completely braindead. This is what I picture your mech pilots thinking: "Hmmm.... Should I, an autogun mech that cannot damage air targets stay here, at the choke point my commander selected for me when there will be another wave of infantry soon, or should I chase the bomber that I have absolutely no way of damaging and get eaten by it? I think I'll chase the bomber!"
-Medical units are notably faster than primary fighting units. This does not sound like a con until you have to micromanage a squad of 10 medic units to actually stay BEHIND your frontline so they dont get pulverized and leave your primary force without a way to repair its armor
-The tower defence mode is very poorly executed. If you make one single mis-move, or even mismanage your resources in the slightest, you will nearly instalose. In addition, if I had wanted to play a TD game, I would have played a TD game.
I feel that this game has a massive amount of potential, but the current issues are, for me at least, completely game breaking. Most notable is the friendly unit AI issues. They will literally chase enemy units half way across the map even if they are not equipped to damage them.
If during development these issues are patched, I would wholeheartedly recommend this game, but as it stands now, I cannot.

Go to your documents folder (under C:\Users\[insert name here]\Documents\WWE2K16) and go into the config.ini file. Once in it, change simple_lighting to on and then change audience_tessellation to off. It's not perfect because it will turn (current day) Sting and Luke Harper into black silhouettes during their entrances. However, if you go to into "advanced creation" for Luke and Sting's entrances, change the lighting to whatever lighting you want and it'll make the character models look normal again. However, I never had any frame rate drops during matches.

This game is probably the most disliked in the series by fans of the souls series, and I have to agree with many of the points raised by people who dislike this game. However, this is far from a bad game, but the first Dark Souls set such a high standard that it would have been extremely difficult to please everyone. But the game definitely still needs to be played, it has some really memorable moments and boss fights, and if you're into PvP it was definitely improved from the first game.
But I have to agree with a lot of fans when they say that there's definitely "something" that's just missing from the sequel.
The world of Dark Souls 1 was just incredible, one of the best designed worlds in gaming, I can still go back and play the game now and still love the world, the atmosphere, the amazing design, I've replayed it so many times. The entire world of the 1st game felt connected, there were shortcuts and secrets littered throughout, however DS2 goes in a different direction. Instead of having the world feel "connected", you will be warping from bonfire to bonfire a lot,  which really takes something away from what made the first game great, and made the world feel natural and beautifully designed.
I remember finishing DS2 for the first time and having absolutely no desire to play it again, the only reason I'm playing it through again now is because of the DLC which I never got on console. I replayed the first game several times on console without any of the DLC, and played through it twice again when I got the Prepare to Die edition on PC. It was just an amazing experience that felt naturally challenging.
On the subject of challenge, Dark Souls 2 is definitely difficult, but it just feels "forced" and very lazy at times, not to mention extremely cheap, and not in the fun "lol dark souls" way, I mean the "♥♥♥♥ the lazy devs who made this dumb boss/mob enemy section" kind of way.
The first game actually never really made me frustrated, because the difficulty felt so natural, I knew I was doing something wrong. (Except for that ♥♥♥♥ing giant dragon bodies in bright orange lava section in Lost Izalith, which even the developers admitted was rushed and a mistake.)
DS2 has many areas where the developers just seem to get extremely lazy and throw in mobs of enemies, it doesn't feel challenging, it just feels frustrating and extremely cheap when you get swarmed by 5 or 6 large enemies in one area, it's a real motivation killer for continuing the game, particularly for a returning player who really just wants to play for the DLC. There's a difference between well designed challenge, and just throwing a ♥♥♥♥ load of enemies in a small room or choke point, and telling the players to deal with the developers laziness "because dark souls".
That's probably my biggest personal gripe with this game, the laziness of a few of the more frustrating sections.
But even with it's flaws, it's still a great ♥♥♥♥ing game, that I would recommend you should play at least once. Great combat and atmosphere, and when the difficulty is done well, it has that feeling of accomplishment when you do finally kill a boss, or get past that one area that keeps messing you up.
In my opinion, you shouldn't go into the game expecting it to be as good or even better than the first, because I don't think it is. But this game is really great in it's own right, and deserves to be played at least once.

Published and  developed by Anatoliy Loginovskikh, The Big Elk is a top down shooter that mixes RPG elements within the gameplay. The game soon turns into a hectic shooter, that makes you run around avoid getting hit but trying to kill the enemies at the same time.
From the trailer of the game, it looks like a very fast paced hectic, top down shooter that requires a lot of precision and well timed shots in order to win. There are some tower defence elements that are mixed into this game as well as a few weapon types that you can pick up to kill enemies that are in your way. For a game like this, you would expect there to be unlimited ammunition. But this game takes a different turn, it requires you to be careful with where you shoot and requires you to be careful with your ammo consumption, this does mean that sometimes you will be running around and you might not find any ammunition for a while. There is a decent amount of areas that you can gain access after you have completed a few levels in order to progress through to the next stage.
The game does a nice job at setting out the tutorial at the beginning of the game. It does well with telling you how each mechanic works in the tutorial, teaching you the basics and once you have completed the tutorial your path is open to the actual levels that you can play. The game seems to be partly nonlinear, the player is given a option to complete the levels in whatever order they want. Obviously, not all the levels are instantly unlocked, but there is some choice in the levels that you can play as you unlock them throughout the game. The enemies that you fight are rather humorous at times and can be rather wild at times, sometimes I was even unsure what these enemies where. For some reason this game reminds me of the classic game on the N64 called Fur Fighters, although I doubt that most of you have heard of that game. It's a little similar to this game but for me it reminded me of that game.
I love the simplistic art style for this game, the game's graphics represent the way that the game is played and is usually the first thing that most players look upon when playing the game. It's simplistic art style and frame animation is well designed, along with the enemies frame animations that are well presented, but the main focus would be upon the player.
The music and sound of this game seem to be well fairly crisp and well designed for this type of game. Although the music at times did seem a little out of place for the type of gameplay that this game is trying to be.
+ Slightly nonlinear gameplay
+ A well made game
+ Lots of weapons to use
+ Steam Achievements & Trading Cards
- Sometimes too limited ammunition
To summarize, The Big Elk is a fast paced RPG top down shooter with a small amount of tower defence elements mixed into the game at various points in the game. The gameplay has limited ammunition, that can sometimes be a downfall to the game as you may be running around looking for some. Other than that the game is rather fun and addicting to play, I would possibly like to see maybe a local multiplayer co-op option as the game progresses through it's early access stage.

The Big Elk is the Steam debut by Anatoliy Loginovskikh. In the summer Anatoliy is a sheep herder and during the winter when the weather is too cold to do that job he becomes a game designer. That might sound a little funny to some of you but to me that sounds like a cool life. Although this is his first game on Steam he has created other games in the past. He claims to have a very old computer that doesn’t allow him to make videos for his games and this would explain the simplicity of them.
Simplicity at its best can generate fascinating games that are open to a broad audience. Though it’s still in early access I believe that that is the case with The Big Elk. It’s a top-down shooter with animal themes that suits Anatoliy’s background. It’s a clever take on the genre that contains a number of elements, varied enemy types and a number of different tools that you can utilize to your benefit in taking down the enemy.
Each area has a number of different game zones that you need to successfully complete in order to progress through to the next one. Once you complete one part of the game more areas of the game open up to you to play. I believe that players also have options in which level they play next – some of the time. There is a smart tutorial at the beginning of the game that does a good job of teaching players the basics and once completed starts you on your path by opening up the first non-tutorial level of the game.
I do like the art style in the game. Although it is the telltale sign of how simple the game is at its core it is immaculately presented and is pleasing to the eyes. The music while not quite as good as the graphics is more than suitable for the game. The biggest problem with the game at the moment is that there may be too little ammunition offered in the game – I run through the ammo that I have very quickly and/or things take longer to kill than what you have ammo for, whichever way you choose to look at it). The other issue that I have with the game is that you cannot change any options (e.g. turn volume up or down, etc.) within the game. These are the two areas that I would work on aside from making the game more Steamified by adding trading cards and achievements (which according to the dev himself are on the way).
This is a game suitable for people of all ages because there is no gore and the action that is in the game is very basic. At its price its a good buy and one that fans of shooters should try.

The Big Elk is a casual, fun and rather unique top down shooter where you play as an Elk
trying to protect his forest homeland from various invaders.  Some of these invaders include gun totting Christmas trees, penguins, Jello molds and other interesting and humorous enemies.  This isn't your mommy and daddies
Rocky and Bullwinkle, this is like Rambo and Bullwinkle had a child who slaughters Christmas themed enemies at any time of the year, with impunity.  While I played the game I threw my voice to talk like Sylvester Stallone in some of his more memorable roles..  like "You can take my life, but you can never take my freedom!!",
My actual quotes while I played were more along the lines of "Stop or my mom will shoot" and Adrian...   Anyway
Being that it's a top down shooter (with tower defense elements) you roll around one of three types of weapons, a Blunderbus shooting drumsticks, a rocket spewing rocket launcher and the penultimate carrot chain gun, the gun play and movements are fluid, the sounds are decent enough, and I'd say it would be a pretty safe bet to allow younger kids to play without much fear, as you aren't using bullets, real guns, nor are any of the enemies other humans.  The total and utter lack of blood also doesn't hurt in the young kid playing department.
The game has 10 game zones, which are broken up into smaller little zones, where you have various task to complete, some are as mundane as going from left to right, others require you to go hog-wild and mow down hordes of enemies, whether they be slimes, meat pies, even some Jello Molds,  while some others may see you dodging various enemies or blasting through piles of ice or rock.
Silky smooth movements
good gun play
decent sounds which
challenging yet surprisingly casual game-play
casual pick up and play type game
Lack of controller support (this can be a positive to some, but I'm a controller fanatic)
I want some Moose/Elk Trading cards dang it..
This can be a fun game experience that can be enjoyed by just about everyone.  While not the most overly complex game, The Big Elk has a charm about it, maybe it's the cute looking creatures, or the obvious Christmas themed enemies, after playing the game it will grow on you...
and you'll soon find yourself thinking about playing it when you aren't.. Eventually you'll stand to do moose calls in your basement and try to speak with animals like in the movie Brother Bear.  I'd say pick it up if you are a fan of casual games or have a child you want to get into video games without fear of having them turn into a brainless zombie who goes on a murderous rampage later on in life.
So if you have a couple of bucks just wasting away in your steam wallet, and like myself can't find anything to play, give The Big Elk a try, just remember to be gentle, the forest creatures are your friends.  SIKE!!! KILL THEM ALL!!!

10 Second Ninja X is an action platformer game, developed by Four Circle Interactive and published by Curve Digital, releasing on PC, PS4 Vita and Xbox One in July 2016. The previous game in the series, 10 Second Ninja which was widely accepted by players as being an arcade style rushing title.
Ninja X takes on the same gameplay aspects as the first. You play as a ninja (oddly enough) and you have to take out various enemies in a timely fashion whilst traversing sometimes deadly platforming stages. The game is partly a sequel to the first, but also an improved version too. You can take out enemies either by using the ninja’s katana or throwing knives. Each level must be completed within 10 seconds, again the devs are really good at naming their game here…! The fast paced game play means you will continously fail a level until everything just clicks into place perfectly and you have your route planned out to a tee. I must warn you though 10 Second Ninja X is a very rage inducing game, there were times when I had to step away from the keyboard just to take a minute to breathe before starting again. You will easily become infuriated at the punishingly difficult stages combined with the 10 second time limit.
The game also has a gating system, so you can’t just simply breeze through the game by only just passing each stage by completing it in 9.50 seconds; you have to earn a substantial amount of stars in order to get onto the next stage of levels. I believe on average it works out as needing to get a 2 star rating on each stage which is by no means an easy feat. I struggled with getting one most of the time!  A huge benefit to the game is that it is very easy to reset a level, if you mess up right at the start you can reset the stage instantly; this can sometimes be a bad thing though as I found myself resetting the level when I didn’t mean to.
Ninja X has the same art style as the first, very crisp looking cartoon graphics which looks just gorgeous. The character sprites are also very well designed and easily one of the best aspects of the visual look to the game. Environments are bright and vibrant with colour and different tones which gives you a sense of exploration throughout the game too. Soundtracks and sound effects are brilliant too; they keep in with the theme as being fast and chaotic giving you that complete immersion effect.
As I said above, the game is gruesomely hard, and every second counts towards the greater goal. Sometimes the path that you need to take to complete a stage may seem completely obvious, but that is not always the best route, you need to be a patient fellow in order to beat this game, I am a mere peasant and only on the second stage and you can see just by the amount of hours I have already put into this game that it is in no way an easy task to manage. You can watch hints and tips from Youtube videos online in order to find the best path, but actually executing them is another task in itself.
The game will have a large amount of replayability even after you manage the mammoth task of 100 levels, you can go back and try your best to three star each level and compete with friends on the leaderboards. If you find this game to be right up your street, prepare yourself for a bargain in terms of $ to hour ratio.
I only had one technical issue, and that was with the game not picking up my controller straight away. For some reason whenever I booted the game up, it would think the active controller would be “port 3” which isn’t exactly helpful as you have to change this manually to “Port 1” in order to get your controller to work. Pro tip; don’t even attempt this game if you don’t have a controller.
10 Second Ninja X is an improved version over the original game in every way. You won’t really miss much skipping the first game, $10.99 for a game of this quality and amount of content is easily a fair price to pay. It definitely will only appeal to a certain audience so I would advise people try out the demo before you make the plunge in purchasing the full game.
