Score: 80	 Author: geekl33tgamer	 Test Drive Unlimited Reddux?
From the outset, the core concept of the game seems very appealing to anyone who has ever picked up a copy of any recent Need for Speed title, or the poorly executed (but great idea) Test Drive Unlimited game. Here we have a huge sprawling online world, filled with literally thousands of players, all going about their own thing with a Need for Speed and Burnout inspired driving model.
The games career play is a very cinematic affair, and within the first few minutes of starting the game you’ll soon start to understand how this game’s style will play itself out. You start off with some cut-scenes of a chase which you get thrown into, this is basically your tutorial. You need to race to the checkpoint marker whilst keeping the vehicle pointing in the general direction. It was certainly a very entertaining start to a game if ever there was one.
You get taken to a garage, meet some key characters who set the scene for the plot in the career play, and you need to buy a car. To begin, you only have a selection of 4 cars to buy, and once you have chosen one your given brief tutorials to the tuning system, car upgrades, perk points and such. There’s not a lot you can buy at this stage, but it’s handy to remember where these things are for later when you have enough cash.
You then begin your journey, working undercover for the FBI whilst infiltrating the 510 car faction. So as not to spoil it for anyone, we shall not go on any further about the plot within The Crew as may are still playing through it, or may not have purchased it yet.
When you have a required first few events of the tutorial / prologue out the way, you are free to play The Crew however you wish. You can crack on with the career play, or so exploring. This is where you get your first look at the seemingly huge map that you have to play in. It is littered with icons of all the events you can do, your friends positions are shown as well as the major cities.
Our first thoughts were that the map is very, very large – however we quickly found out that it isn’t. Despite appearing large, we can drive from the east coast to the west in a little over an hour. Missions as you play them will move you over most of it, but we felt a little disappointed it wasn’t as expansive as the map from Test Drive Unlimited for example. It doesn’t feel too small neither, but isn’t as unwieldy as it first appears to be.
As you explore the world, between events on literally every road are skill events you can just drive into at full speed to activate a mini-challenge. This helps break up the monotonous task of driving long distances between places, and gives you extra cash to spend in-game as well as car parts and experience points. Once you’ve explore enough areas, the game has a fast travel feature so you can easily jump back to anywhere you’ve previously been. If you discover the airports and train stations, you can also use these.
The major US cities litter the map, and the world is busy with jots of NPC traffic filling up the places. The cities never really feel big enough, but we understand the compromises that they had to make here to a point. Each city has a unique vibe and appearance. The mountain sections look particularly impressive, as does the games day and night cycle. It creates a great environment overall.
There are 4 cars to start with, but you can purchase any of the others as you discover new garages on the map. New garages unlock new classes of cars, but for a car game the total amount of cars we counted was only 45. We know Ubisoft plan to add more (with a season pass, sold extra), but the amount in the game does seem disappointing.
Of the cars that are in there, they are nicely replicated visually. Each car you buy can be upgraded and tuned into different cars to suit your environment or event. Almost all the cars can be upgraded to street spec, performance, track, dirt and raid classes. The latter 2 are heavy duty modifications that make your car great off road, while the others lend themselves well to road racing. You can customize most visual areas of the car, upgrade its engine parts, and add decals. It adds enough to the car customization to make the cars to make them feel like they are personally yours, but the tuning options do not go deep enough for some. The upgrade parts are fixed, so you can buy varying grades of better brakes, or a differential, but you can’t tweak them if you wanted to say shift the brake bias forward.
Perhaps the limiting of the granularity in the tuning area is deliberate so the game is more accessible. We don’t mind it as it does offer enough, but I know from speaking to players while racing, some were not happy with it. They equally wasn’t thrilled by the cars handling model. It is very much in the arcade category, but we expected that. It makes the game enjoyable to zoom around and have fun without needing to pay too much attention to corner entry lines and braking – Instead you can hone your skills on seeing how high you can jump off the ski-slope for example.
Now, this is perhaps the game’s biggest selling point, and in Ubisoft’s own words they say “You’ll never drive alone”. I need to make it clear from the get go that this game does not have all the Uplay problems that come with Watch Dogs at launch, or any of the other recent titles released – However there are still problems.
We had no problems getting into the servers on launch day, despite the large surge of traffic, but the connection reliability has been ropy from time to time while playing. Without any warning whatsoever, if your connection drops for even a second, you’re returned to your desktop with an error message about the servers not being reached. That is coupled with the fact that every time it does this, some of your game progress gets lost. When you re-load the game, you will invariably find yourself many miles from where you actually were when it threw you out. This unfortunately happens with varying frequency, but it is something they are aware of so we hope it improves.
Another widely touted feature was the ability to form a Crew on the fly from either your friends or others who are in the world with you. Crews are important to help with the co-op options available in most missions – Some are quite difficult to do on your own, so pulling in others is an easier way to beat that one mission you may have been stalled on.
Sadly, we encountered several problems with this that could easily take up most of this review. We had problems adding friends into Uplay first off, and getting the game to recognize them in the game so I could add them. All too often friends in Uplay would not appear within the game itself. When they did, getting them added to the crew is simply an exercise of luck. Constant errors and timeout’s hampered forming a Crew on the fly as intended, and I found myself driving around by myself a lot of the time as a result. It’s currently near impossible to add players who are in a different country to yourself too, and this frustrate me further.
As a final nail in the coffin where online play is concerned, if you have the game in Steam as we do, you can’t invite your Steam friends into a game at all. You need to ask your friend for their Uplay ID, try and add them and then go through the process above.
I feel players who buy into the game expecting a racing simulator should steer well clear, but if Need for Speed and Burnout style games are your thing, we think you’ll love The Crew. We do.

I have a love hate relationship with this game. Before the anti-cheat went in place I left because most games I played there was obvious cheating like people killing you with a knife even though they are still standing in their spawning spot on the other side of the map (just look up youtube videos to see such stuff). Since they have put the anti-cheat in place, cheats are no longer frequent although there is still the occasional obvious cheat happening.
For the most part there are lots of excellent gamers in the warface community who make this fun whether playing with noobs or other experienced players - simply put you can have a good time and a lot of laughs.  But that is changing...
There are two major problems to this game. First there are some serious OP weapons and armor available if you got the money...(but apparently not as OP as some stuff offered and accumulated by players when cheats were still allowed - and although those are rarely found on the auction site...players still have them).  That in itself is not bad, as I was still able to kill OP players, it just took more work and skill. Because I could still kill OP players I believed skill had more to do with winning that the OP weapons. But more and more frequently I was running into OP players that were pretty much indestructible and sadly more and more often they are often also incredibly arrogant and rude to everyone.
The occassional rude player doesn't usually get to me but this is where things changed for me. I started picking up the dropped OP weapon when these players were finally killed and using their weapon I could go from one of the average players on the team to the top position and I was just using default armor. For example, I could with a shotgun kill a sniper in the distance (could barely see them) without aiming in two shots.  At first it felt good I could start being in top position a lot more often and it felt really good killing those OP players over and over with their own dropped gun, but as my skill level had not changed in anyway, it clearly showed me the weapon makes a lot bigger difference than I had ever imagined. And that was just the OP gun. Many top players also have OP armor, knifes, even repair kits. The only way to really get these OP items is to pay a lot of money to get them and keep them repaired. Or pay even more money for a gold weapons as they never need repairing.
My other big concern is there is lots of lag recently. I have a very fast fibre network but there are not many server locations (USA, Europe, and Turkey) and the fastest ping times I get to the nearest server (US) is 70ms. I have also noticed it isn't just me...in each game at least 80% of the players are only getting 2 or less bars (out of 5) for signal speed and of those most are only getting 1 bar. In a game of 16 players it is not unusual to see only one player with 4 bars, one with 3 bars, 5 or so with 2 bars and the rest 1 or 0 bars.
Interestingly, I've also noticed the player with 4 bars is often in the top position on the leaderboard at the end of the game. They often get called out for cheating as they often shoot you before they even come around the corner so it seems like they are shooting through walls but I'm pretty sure this is lag. The reality is the lag creates a problem where they know where you and you only think you know where you are. That gives them a serious advantage and unlike me being able to pick up a dropped OP weapon...there is NOTHING I can do to fix this.  The lag has been so problematic in the last few weeks that I'm seeing it create other problems too such as seeing players (including myself) fall through floors, crossing the room 2 or more times before you actually can get out of the room, etc. I even watched while a player was in prone position get shot standing even though he went prone (and out of line of sight) at least 3 seconds prior...I was repairing their armor when they disappeared and then re-appeared standing but shot/dead. So basically shot him on their screen before he laid down even though on this and my screen he was already laying down.
If the player with the least amount of lag is also OP, you might as well just leave the game....which I have been doing more and more frequently.
Sadly the other thing I see changing is most games were fun where people had a lot of fun with each other...but I'm noticing a lot of arrogant and just mean spirited OP players (and clans) as of late that are taking the fun out of it for a lot of new players I've recruited (well me too). I saw and article that said a recent survey of people in the USA are becoming increasingly more rude publically and angry...the article blamed it on their election so maybe once the election is done and they fix the lagging this game might be worth trying again. As for now I'm recommending to my friends they don't get into this game.

10 SECOND NINJA X is a blisteringly fast, overwhelmingly intense action game. The nefarious Captain Greatbeard has kidnapped you and trapped your forest friends inside of his army of robots like some kind of psychopath. Greatbeard doesn't think you're the fastest ninja who ever lived - he is WRONG. Destroy all of Greatbeard's robots in each level in ten seconds or less. 21 hours in, The Crew gets a lot of bad hype from the playerbase.
I'm not too sure why. The GRID-2 esque driving is a letdown, of course. But the open map, beautiful car models, and superb level of customization is something that has me getting back on every single day.
Pros -
Massive open world
Detail on the cars, though lack of working rearview mirrors annoys me.
Halfway decent story (It's nothing special, but it's a nice change from your average G.I. Joe who kills everything with two legs and hair where there shouldn't be).
The... Car... Putting itself together... Thing....
Very good performance on my system
Native controller support (it's needed and will probably feel better than a wheel, but that's just a thought).
Tires work like they do in real life. (That's right,  you'd better learn how to nudge around corners instead of drifting every single one).
Cars actually feel different in every single way, from handling, to acceleration, to braking, whether it's 15mph in a Raptor or 145 in a raid spec Mustang.
MMO Aspect - The game's MMO aspect is a dual blessing and curse, as situations like this arise.
Driving down the road in a performance mod Ford Focus RS.
Look up, a player is sitting on the shoulder of the road up ahead.
I pull up next to a Laferrari
Eh, why not? I rev my engine
He revs his. 3 seconds later we shoot off.
45 seconds later we reach my turn and I take it, pulling over.
5 seconds later the Laferrari chugs up the road.
He pauses his game and dissapears.
Things like that can happen. Randomly. It's great, you feel like you're more than a tourist in a fast car with an ugly neck tat.
Long races.
LONG RACES.
I've done races that lasted a full 2 1/2 hours.
2 hours. 30 minutes. 90 minutes. 60 seconds x 90.
I don't care what you're playing. What you're interested in. Where you're from.
Or what year the game was made in.
If you get to the end of a 2.5 hour race it is epic. No matter what.
Non-restrictive racing GPS.
In GTAV I had a problem - I memorized the city and it's routes. I knew shortcuts.
They didn't help for♥♥♥♥♥♥in races with checkpoints every 30 seconds.
In the crew, as long as you hit the next checkpoint (They're often 1-2 minutes away from eachother), you get credit.
Want to cut that corner? No fear, the game won't punish you.
Going down a hill road with a lot of turns, but there's a jump that can get you to the bottom in 3 seconds flat? As long as there's not a checkpoint on the hill road, the game won't punish you.
Want to jump that hill to skip that hard turn? No problem, just watch out for the tree.
Cons -
May not run well on lower-end systems. (My computer is worth about 1300 dollars, and can run everything but anti-aliasing at it's max setttings, and even then, my GPU is mid-tier).
MMO aspect - The MMO aspect to this game is a dual blessing and curse, as situations such as these arise.
Players that park their car on challenge courses, speed and Slalom mainly - You have no choice but to miss your objective or hit the car head on at a generally breakneck speed.
Players that invite you to co-op missions and leave when you start winning, not knowing if you win they still win - You just wasted your time and have nothing to show for it. Because some kid is butmad.
GTA drivers - Kids that ram you every 30 seconds, trying to knock you out of your place because the idea of actually racing to race instead of (theoretically) wasting your thousands of dollar aftermods and paint job on some ninnie who's car is faster. But then again, kids these days haven't been praised for critical thinking.
Useless E-brake - Oh yeah, rage all you want. I've yet to come to any hairpin where pumping or locking my main brakes briefly and using nitrous to straighten out didn't work. And I don't jump down to 20mph like I would popping an E brake turn.
Car fanboys - I don't care that the GTR isn't right-side drive. It's a game. You want "your" GTR to be perfect, you go buy it.
PvP - As an MMO player, I have to say one thing - Screw this PvP. There's no ladder or groupings of people of a simillar level. Once you hit level 10, expect to pvp against people with level 1000+ cars. I tried it once, left and only do co-op missions now. Until they can orgainize the PvP better, my suggestion is to stay away until you yourself have a "min-maxed" car.
Limited (For the moment it seems) car selection -
At the time of this review, an update has been added that added about 5 cars to the game free of charge. I hope we can expect more things like this, as it was a welcome change of pace from paying 10 dollars for 2 models of some Audi I'll never drive but only want because muh car collection
Arcade-y driving - Yeah, it's like the Call of Duty of racing games. You'll live.
TL;DR
Buy it if you think you can run it. If you don't, don't waste your money. You'll need more than a half decent PC build (Entire PC build, not just a GPU. If you're running a pentium it doesn't matter what GPU you have, things are going to mess up).
Don't upgrade your PC to high end status just for this game. It's not THAT great.
Keep Steam online for updates to the game (they don't come from Uplay), otherwise you'll be harassed with error codes.

If you have high expectations of a Command and Conquer or Supreme Commander you may be disappointed but it is still a good game in its own right and fans of the genre should try it out.
Meridian is strongly focused on single player, It has a good storyline spanning over 15 missions and sections between each one where you can interact with and get to know the characters.
You will have to make choices along the way. Your actions will be remembered and change the way things go for you.
New mechanics are introduced throughout the campaign but doesn't forget about being an RTS when that is happening.
Units are limited but instead you get to select the weapons for each unit you train, allowing you to use the unit type and weapon most suited for your situation.
You can also try out several small challenges during the campaign to see how weel you can use each of the units.
There is NO multi-player (Story and Skirmish only - up to 3 AI) so do not buy if that is all you are interested in.
There is only ONE faction (Human) but the weapon customisation allows for up to 100 differnt unit to be created.
The map editor and scripting tool used to make the campaign is available with the game; meaning anyone can create anything seen during the game as well as modify existing units, buildings and soon weapons.
Custom maps can be shared on Steam Workshop so you can make your own content for others or try theirs out giving you endless free content.
It's Easy to use and has a 50 page PDF document to help.
Meridian: New World also has a really nice sound track that fits well.
There are 75 Achievements to work towards if you want give yourself more challenges.
Developer is active in the forums, listens to all suggestions and has a good record for fixing technical issues for people individually.
Community shared maps will continue to provide more and new game play too.

I've played this game previously on the Xbox One. According to the Xbox, I have played at least 264 hours on it.
So how does the PC version stand up to the console version? I think it holds up very well. The game does have a few crashing problems for me, but so did the console version. The PC version also loads up 10x quicker than console. It would literally take a minute or more to load into a match on the console. For PC, it takes about 10 seconds.
If you're looking for an arcade like wrestling game, I'd suggest looking for a different title. But for someone looking to play a wrestling simulation just like the TV show, you will love this game.
The pacing in matches is fairly slow to start off as you perform lock ups. You then transition into your normal grapples, leading into back and forth action. You have limited reversal, so you have to use your reversals wisely. As you get into the big heavy hitting moves, you start to feel the exhaustion as your wrestler fights with every last strength they have. Every time you kick out from a person's finisher, you feel like you're out of breath as you and your opponent can't believe you still have fight left in you. Believe me when I say, you will feel extremely satisfied when you kick out of a finisher without using your resiliency. And honestly, it's hard to get upset after losing a match when you know you put up one h*ll of a show.
For creations mode, you have a decent variety of things to create. You can create your own Wrestler (Cool looking or just plain wacky), you can create your own title belt, your own arena, your own show, and unlike 2K15, you can create your own Woman Wrestler (or Diva, as WWE likes to call them...). The customization for your wrestlers are very good. I have been able to create some very life like wrestlers, especially with the face import tool (where you can import any face you want and use them for your created wrestler). Create a move-set is still there of course. Create an entrance is better this year, with nearly every wrestler's entrance as an option, as opposed to very little. Unfortunately, still no custom themes (but there are mods for that...)

10 seconds ninja x is a puzzle platformer. It’s a sequel to 10 Seconds Ninja which was released back a couple of years ago. In this game you must complete your objective within 10 seconds as the name of the game suggests. This can make for some very fun strategic and twitch gameplay. Not only your jumps/attacks be quick, they must also be accurate and one wrong move will have you starting the stage over again.
The graphics are pretty plain and simple. The game is pretty and nicely colorful. The game is locked at 60 FPS and I got 60 FPS throughout the whole time I played.
The music is okay too. It keeps you entertained. Nothing to write home about. The sound itself is good though, the jumping, sword strikes and the shorukens sound pretty nice.
The game's story is that the evil Captain Greatbeard has kidnapped you and your friends from a forest and into his ship. This is where your adventure begins. The gameplay is very simple. You are a ninja and you must destroy these robots by Captain Greatbeard in each level to progress. You’re given 10 seconds to complete your objective. In between the missions you can go around the ship and talk to other people who have been kidnapped too.
You have jump and double jump. You get a sword weapon and 3 shoryukens which you must use wisely. Not only do you have to be accurate with your movement you must also strategize your kill order. This is very important as a wrong kill order will waste your time. You must figure out the most efficient way to kill the robots. In the later levels new things are introduced such as robots who only die to shoryukens and can kill you if you go near them as they are surrounded by a short electric field, switches which must be pressed in the right order, etc.
Each level costs around 20 stars to activate so you must get at least 2 star score in every stage of the levels. Getting 3 stars can be very difficult as I wasn’t able to get 3 stars in any of the 3 level stages I played so far. Each level contains 10 stages and you can earn stars when you finish the stage. The quicker you are the more stars you get. The game will tell you to beat x number of seconds for the next star level. These stars are important as you cannot progress to the next level until you have the required number of stars.

I've been a huge fan of this game since it came out on PS2 and still love it today.
Let's get the small list of negatives out the window first:
This game was a beautiful game for its time; to be honest, I still think it looks great, not for the technology involved, but the art direction it took. Colors are vibrant and pop out, the character designs are whacky (in a good way), and the music pieces are among some of the best out there in a video game.
The story is pretty simple but deep at the same time. While some people didn't like the main character Tidus, I personally love him. He's a cheerful guy with an extroverted personality; a refreshment from the games where the main character is a complete mute and/or emotionally awkward. The "silent and cool guy" cliche is overused and it's good that Tidus isn't depicted as such, but a loud-mouthed cocky♥♥♥♥♥♥ He pulls his way through and changes a lot as the story progresses, making him one of the more interesting characters in comparison to other FF characters.
Battle/Gameplay is subjective, not everyone is a fan of turn based RPGs so I can't comment much on it. What I can say however, is that FFX has the best leveling system of all Final Fantasy games. For the first half of the game, every character's role is important (except for riku), and you feel that you need to switch out characters depending on the enemies. Although this is negated as you max out your sphere grid and every character performs about the same, the most of the game forces you to carefully choose your skill path if you play on expert sphere grid from the start (which is what I did).
This game is bundled with FFX-2, which in my opinion, is pretty crap - but hey - you might like it if you're into playing with dress ups and watching Sailor Moon's transformations. FFX-2 does have a fun super boss though, so I give it credit for that.
Overall, I can definitely recommend the purchase of this remaster. I haven't detected any major bugs with it, and the drawbacks are fairly minor. This game is a must have for anyone who enjoys a decent JRPG.

While playing through this game a couple things stood out to me. For one the combat system is very fun, felt like a lot of the other FF games I've played in the past as well as Bravely Default, a spiritual successor to the FF games on the 3DS. Unlike other FF games I've played however, you can switch characters in and out at will during battle without taking up turns. The leveling system using the sphere grid was an interesting twist on leveling your characters. I personally prefer the usual type of leveling systems in my games, but the way the sphere grid works, it fits in just fine. In terms of difficulty, this game isn't too hard. A couple bosses might leave you stuck, but that's about it. I didn't find it requiring too much grinding either, so that was pretty nice as well.
The story of FFX was pretty good. Although it didn't really hook me as much as some other players, it was still an enjoyable story overall. I personally really liked the backstory and history of this game, especially of that of Zanarkand, that of the main characters, and of Sin. The music for this game is alright, not amazing, but not too bad either. A couple of the tracks from this game I actually quite enjoyed including one of the final boss fights of whom I won't mention.
In the end, FFX was quite the enjoyable experience for me, and if you're a fan of turn-based RPGs, new or old, then I'd definitely suggest checking this game out.

Homefront: The Revolution is an odd game. It's not odd in a bad way, but it presents itself as that highschool kid that is trying to act like he or she is eccentric for attention, and manages to become really popular either through pity or finesse. This kid later builds up his personality to be someone greater than his/her former self, and people don't recognize him/her in the highschool reunion three decades later because of the mark that was left upon them.
Homefront: The Revolution is a very ambitious game. It tries to implement mechanics from other games, but adds a little bit of disparity to keep you on your toes. On my first playthrough, I wasn't quite sure over how to react to this game because I was conditioned to play a certain way. I thought I would be getting to these outposts once I finish the mission, but each mission continued where it had stopped. On other occasions, you can blow up vehicles and destroy holes with a silenced pistol as long as you have enough ammunition.
Once you get past playing the story, Resistence Mode or the Co-Op Skirmishing is where it's at. If you play this mode, I highly suggest getting one of the DLCs to speed up the process, as you're not Ethan Brady, the silent protagonist, you're the twerp at the edge of the neighborhood. They pretty much strip you barebones and expect you to complete missions with your assault rifle. Of course, I am also looking at this from a solo point of view, so I bet having the extra player can really make or break the game.
If you've played through Far Cry 3/4 and up to the second half of Dying Light, this pretty much sets up the framework over what you'll be doing. The first three hours of gameplay is tutorialization, but it's more of a sandbox before the actual problem hits. There are two main currencies you can spend. One is dollars, which are typically used to purchase gear and base weapons. The other currency is unlocked through capturing outposts or networking stations. These allow you to convert your guns to a different type of gun, or modify your method of approach in hacking, distracting, flaming, or blowing up.
Something that I would urge any player new to the game to do would be to play the game on a harder difficulty. This is not for bragging rights, rather it's more of a way on how quickly you would like to move through the game. I originally played this game on its designated 'medium' mode, and found myself dying on multiple occasions, getting a feel for how powerful the KPA can be, only making my immersion in the game that much stronger. If you play this game on its 'Recruit' Mode, you can kill.. say a heavy from Far Cry 3 with a full clip from a silenced pistol from the front. On the back, two shots are enough.
Much like any other shooter, you're a silent protagonist, but with a name. As Ethan Brady, a lot of the civillians are failed ghouls from Fallout while all of the resistence members and main characters are somewhat conventionally attractive. Even while playing this game, I found myself starting to dislike nearly every character and having no remorse for their deaths. Not that this was a problem on my part, the character player himself simply appears to speak to everyone telepathically.
I will say though, I think my favorite was Dana, She can be very convincing, until Jack slowed her roll. Ned Sharpe, one of the characters in the early game, sounds like the Mega Man 8 Dr. Wahwee voice actor.
I wanted a game that was ... "generic" enough. It's fair to say that some of us want something new in our games, but this was a realization on my part where I wanted this gameplay loop. This gameplay loop of introducing you to a procedurally generated building with various troops and variable AI patterns, and then overcoming it with some finesse. Far Cry 3/4, Dying Light, Just Cause, MGSV:TPP.. They all have the same pattern, and it's what I enjoy.
Also, for anyone who wants to see a bit of some TimeSplitters 2 action, you can play the first two story missions in the restricted zone near the bourse. The port was done by the original TimeSplitters team, and it handles itself pretty well. (Press [Reload] on the Radar to play Andaconda)

Complete and total revamp to many of the areas, enemies, bosses, and combat of DS2 while fixing many of the problems of the original DS2.  They removed several of the problems ailing the vanilla game and strengthened many of the other parts by, adding more enemies, adding new enemies, adding more secrets, adding more equipment, and nerfing some of the extreme problems of the PvP.  Top it off with having all three DLC's and you've got yourself a game with at least a good 50 hours in it for the average person.
Even if you played the original version of this game, buy this version.  There are so many new things that is will feel like playing almost an entirely new game.  Just watch as you stroll by the tutorial into the first area and notice some major differences in enemy types and locations of said enemies.  Even if you know an area of the vanilla game like the back of your hand you will still die going through that same area in SotFS.
Completely worth the money, especailly if you get it on sale.  If you are a veteran to the series, buy this one instead of the vanilla game, it will satisfy you much more as it is almost exactly what people were hoping that would come after the original Dark Souls.  If you are new to the Souls Series then this is probably the one to start at as well.  From here you can easily branch off into the playstyles of all of the different Souls games, from DS1 to DS3 to Demon Souls and even to Bloodborne as it took some inspiration from DS2 itself.
While it may not be the pinnacle of the series in most people's eyes, it is definitely an experience worth having and should most definitely be played by anyone who is looking to get into the Souls series.

Verdun is the best depiction of world war one in any game to date. While some developers might change substantially history when building a game based on an old war (to give players better guns, for instance), it didn't happen here. Instead, the game only takes the liberties needed for the interest of gameplay, such as mixing nations in a single trench.
The weapons, the uniforms, the battlefield, even the "rules" of trench warfare are authentic. Playing Verdun feels like playing a world war one version of Red Orchestra that would be adapted to trench warfare. So it's hard, it's unforgiving, it makes you crawl through trenches, aim carefully and throw grenades tactically. Despite the crudeness of the weapons, there is a lot of variety between bolt-action rifles (each with their own quirks), machine guns, pistols, shotguns and even a few submachine guns of the era. The variety also shows in the maps, between the lush woods of the Vosges, the hard concrete of Fort Douaumont and the mud of the trenches of Champagne.
While the game isn't visually jaw-dropping, it has its charm through its detailled visuals and restrained use of effects. The sound design, while not ground-breaking, is also really good and helps sell the atmosphere of the game.
Any history buff looking to experience world war one will enjoy this game, as well as people looking for gritty multiplayer tactical shooters.

This game is probably the most disliked in the series by fans of the souls series, and I have to agree with many of the points raised by people who dislike this game. However, this is far from a bad game, but the first Dark Souls set such a high standard that it would have been extremely difficult to please everyone. But the game definitely still needs to be played, it has some really memorable moments and boss fights, and if you're into PvP it was definitely improved from the first game.
But I have to agree with a lot of fans when they say that there's definitely "something" that's just missing from the sequel.
The world of Dark Souls 1 was just incredible, one of the best designed worlds in gaming, I can still go back and play the game now and still love the world, the atmosphere, the amazing design, I've replayed it so many times. The entire world of the 1st game felt connected, there were shortcuts and secrets littered throughout, however DS2 goes in a different direction. Instead of having the world feel "connected", you will be warping from bonfire to bonfire a lot,  which really takes something away from what made the first game great, and made the world feel natural and beautifully designed.
I remember finishing DS2 for the first time and having absolutely no desire to play it again, the only reason I'm playing it through again now is because of the DLC which I never got on console. I replayed the first game several times on console without any of the DLC, and played through it twice again when I got the Prepare to Die edition on PC. It was just an amazing experience that felt naturally challenging.
On the subject of challenge, Dark Souls 2 is definitely difficult, but it just feels "forced" and very lazy at times, not to mention extremely cheap, and not in the fun "lol dark souls" way, I mean the "♥♥♥♥ the lazy devs who made this dumb boss/mob enemy section" kind of way.
The first game actually never really made me frustrated, because the difficulty felt so natural, I knew I was doing something wrong. (Except for that ♥♥♥♥ing giant dragon bodies in bright orange lava section in Lost Izalith, which even the developers admitted was rushed and a mistake.)
DS2 has many areas where the developers just seem to get extremely lazy and throw in mobs of enemies, it doesn't feel challenging, it just feels frustrating and extremely cheap when you get swarmed by 5 or 6 large enemies in one area, it's a real motivation killer for continuing the game, particularly for a returning player who really just wants to play for the DLC. There's a difference between well designed challenge, and just throwing a ♥♥♥♥ load of enemies in a small room or choke point, and telling the players to deal with the developers laziness "because dark souls".
That's probably my biggest personal gripe with this game, the laziness of a few of the more frustrating sections.
But even with it's flaws, it's still a great ♥♥♥♥ing game, that I would recommend you should play at least once. Great combat and atmosphere, and when the difficulty is done well, it has that feeling of accomplishment when you do finally kill a boss, or get past that one area that keeps messing you up.
In my opinion, you shouldn't go into the game expecting it to be as good or even better than the first, because I don't think it is. But this game is really great in it's own right, and deserves to be played at least once.

It's hard to review this kind of game because I both liked it and didn't like it at the same time. I liked exploring the house, grabbing everything and making a mess of the place. I like games that let me interact with the environment and make a huge mess of the area. I also liked the atmosphere that the game provided. You're in a big, dark house by yourself while a storm is happening outside. It's a little spooky, wandering around looking to turn all the lights on.
Despite that though, the story was so-so to me. Maybe it was because the game was so short (It took me a bit over 2 hours, and that was with being stuck for 30-40 minutes), so it felt rushed, and I wish more things had been touched upon. Though you play as Katie, the story mostly centers towards her little sister Sam, a teenage girl
.
The game focuses around Sam and her
. At time's it's cute and kind of sad, but for the most part, it comes off as angsty and obnoxious because, well, they're teenagers, and teenagers are usually full of angst. The game also touches on the parents lives, but I found it hard to fully follow what happened, because it felt mostly over-shadowed by the whole Sam storyline. I wish the game had given us a deeper look into how they dealt with everything going on in their lives. You got bits of what they went through, but nowhere near as touched upon as Sam's life, what she went through, and how she felt about it all. I know it was a game about Sam, but I hate that almost everyone else fell to the side in terms of characterization.
I wish that Katie had been more explored upon as well. She's who you play as, but I felt like you don't know that much about her. She's a 22 year old girl who has
, and that's about it. No explanation about who she was or why she was even gone in the first place.
All in all, the game was fun to play. As previously mentioned, I do wish it had been longer, if only to give more story behind how the parents felt about everything going on, and to tell us more about Katie. I know it was a game about Sam, but I found her insufferable at times. I was gifted the game, but despite it, I feel like 20 dollars is a high price for what you get. Even 10 dollars would be a stretch. I don't regret playing at all, but I also don't feel that the story is compelling enough to warrant the price of the game.

This game lacks in quite a lot of strategy, and rather depends on how you manipulate the AI into making your odds favorable, whether that be deploying a decoy and making your enemy destroy their base for you, or throwing a few good cans of tear gas and mercilessly gunning down your enemy, the actual "strategy" involved is pretty fire-and-forget.
At times I've wanted to be able to micromanage my troops more, such as moving them out of the way of incoming enemy missiles or abilities in general - and this is where the game can feel the most restrictive, as you have very little interaction except the units and abilities you choose to use.
Despite the game's lack of strategic depth, it has a lot of charm and addictive qualities to it, which I for one am a fan of. The customisation of units, leveling up units and adding perks for them, having challenges and unlocks to buff them permanently all seem like good initiatives for the player to grind and earn. Despite this, however, I've never felt my troops have had an edge or had a disadvantage compared to my enemies. The game's base-building, although a little rough around the edges, definitely shows potential.
While I can appreciate the game is a free-to-play, there are some glooming issues that the game has due to a lack of attention to detail, or the lack of the right man being paid the right amount of money to do the right job. For example, a lot of munitions prices (the in-game currency to level-up structures and purchase new units) are ridiculously high, even if you pay for the funds. Another thing I perceive as an oversight (or perhaps another limitation of the game) are the attack waves. A lot of the AI attacks on your base will be a spam of the same RPG unit that seems to do good AoE damage to infantry and accurate long-range damage to your structures. While weak individually due to your masses of grunts, in the late game when you are facing waves of these, it can feel lazy and a lack of unit variety within these waves really makes them a chore.
Despite all of this, however, I find GUNS UP an enjoyable title. For a free game, I've received a lot of the premium stuff (dynamite, valor, gold) just from playing the game and winning battles and daily missions. I feel I could easily continue playing the game for another week or two whenever I'm bored and progress through it just fine without purchasing anything. (And, due to the fact you can challenge both lower and higher leveled players, this doesn't necessarily make the game P2W as you will most likely be paired with people around your level).
I like this game and the quirks it has to offer, though I'd love to see it ironed out and perfected.

A glorified mobile game? Possibly. But is it made with quite some depth, satisfying gameplay, good looking style, good animations, nice mechanics, and rewards you kindly? Definetly. While its quite unnusual that not only we receive a PS4 port of this game here for some reason, aswell as this kind of game made for PS4, it certainly is a welcome addition to the steam store, game quite unexpectedly appeared out of nowhere and a friend of mine by just playing it, has motivated me to try it and its quite good. Now it has the mechanics and pacing of a mobile game, you build a base made of defenses, you raid other players for resources to advance and to earn a higher spot on the leaderboards, you work with a alliance, you unlock more and more new and better type of troops to use, you upgrade said troops, you spend time trying to make the best defense, you proggress by leveling up and upgrading, you have your hero units, etc. But with slightly more depth added to it, more ways and modes to play the game, not exactly having the type of troops youd expect elsewhere for the most part, not bothering you over multiple types of resources, just one, offering the best customization options thus far that...realy isnt in any game of this genre/type, actualy offering CPU raids against you and encouraged aswell for rewards, and with the already familiar kind of gameplay so quite well refined but with twists such as the different playing field, its a pretty neat game, rather fun, enjoyable so far, plenty of changes have been and are being made to acommadate the game for the pc, with a handfull of activities and plenty of goals worked on by a potentialy dependable team, mobile game or not, its a good game if it brings fun and motivation to keep coming back for more, which to me it does, and with the saddly departure of Warfare Online, who and what else can honestly fill that void these days other than GUNS UP! ? Like it in the end or not, its a realy good game to atleast try, its free, its not big and hints at big content updates ive noticed can only improve it already from a pretty good start here on steam. Its not exactly a typical RTS per say, but it can fill a void of some particular nieche you might have. Pluss, lets remember, this is a PS4 port, not of a game we all wanted, but a game that can be the stepping stones of those games to come, so give it a chance, its nothing demanding or consuming other than your time, if you enjoy it, please commend it then, pass word, rating and references, help the game and wish the devs good luck, its a good game, absolutely cannot complain, except for two very much needed features currently lacking. Allow me to fast forward the replays so i can get trough them quicker, i can perfectly finely watch at twice the speed but dont stop there. And maybe let us have more control over our sandbags, like, let us assign things to them, maybe give control over the red barrels that we could make somehow detonate by something automated, and let us be able to upgrade those bags, im sure they can be. And make the transport truck have a bigger presence on the battlefield, maybe give it more range and a bit more damage but DEFINETLY make it so it keeps moving and NEVER stops, give it maybe a supportive role or something like that, i just dont like that it has a mounted gun but doesnt help your troops, oh and also ALLOW us to utilize the vast empty space under our HQ, theres so much room we can use but for some reason it appears to be allocated for our veterans to just hang around with, why such a waste of space? But other than that i love the design of everything from grunts to walls, the sound design, the music design, the animations, i love the personalized looks you can give, even the most basic ones, the strategies you can make for defense and attack that you will definetly have to start thinking of eventualy as its only going to get harder on both defense and offense, the amount of gore the game doesnt shy from showing in a war game after all, soldiers being blown up in the air with all the pyshics is satisfying, all in all a great game, nothing AAA worthy as balance could probably be talked a whole lot more, not that i would know excesivly alot or considerably enough, but realy honestly quite a good title, i am thankfull for whoever tought of porting this from PS4 to here, because oh, theres also crossplay between us and the console players so thats realy nice & good. The game has potential, it's cute, but there are annoying things. If they improve it with more features, buildings, units, and make it more player friendly, it could be a much better game.
First of all, they say it's "Pay-to-Grow-Faster", so i'm playing for free and after 163 hours, i'm close to level 34 (there is a total of 200 levels). The exp boosts are not so useful, the exp is still hard, except if you are so rich to use a million of boosts.
At the end of every match there is a chance to get rewarded with Attacks Cards, with chests, or with Keys (used to open chests - you need 10-25 Keys to open chests), or with Valor Points to upgrade your units (every unit is upgradable three times), or with very rare drops like Epic Card packs (and maybe Legendary Packs, but personally i didn't find any Legendary).
Attack Cards are consumables like bombs, bonus speed for your units, bonus damage etc... that you can use during your attacks.
You can't play direct-PvP: you can attack player bases and they can't defend, but just watch your attack through a replay and choose to start a retaliation.
What's inside chests? There are different chests. Some item is guaranteed, some item is random.
Helmets (helmets give you some bonus), Valor Points, Build Points, special units etc... etc... or Hero Perks is what you could find inside chests. As i said at level 34 i didn't find Hero Perks, but i have found special units. With more luck you could find a couple of Hero Perks and a couple of special units by opening chests from level 1 to level 34, but the chests that contain them require 25 Keys, or Golds (real money), so you can't really open many chests with Keys.
I don't know if it's possible dropping Hero Perks as PvP rewards, or if the chests are the only way to find them, but i suppose it's possible as i have found an Epic Card Pack against a lowbie player, and you can receive even better rewards by beating stronger players (the rating of their strength goes from 1-Skull to 3-Skulls, and from 1-Skull Nightmare to 3-Skulls Nightmare).
So, the annoying things are the powerful Hero Perks as you require many Hero Perks for all your units... the grinding, which is very, very, very, very, VERY SLOW (it's not only negative, as it adds longevity to the game), and the Alliance Battles.
Alliance Battles is an event, like a season, where you can attack other players to earn points for your clan.
All players have three free daily Alliance Battles. When you are out of dailies, you can fight again for your alliance by paying with Golds, so you can pay with real money to buy Golds and fight more battles for your Alliance, earn more points and win the season, or you can farm by attacking players to earn points that are used to unlock more Alliance Battles (e.g.: after 100 points you unlock one more Alliance Battle - after 160 points you unlock another Alliance Battle and so on).
It's clear that's Pay-to-Win as you can buy golds and play more Alliance Battles, but the rewards at the end of the season are not essentials. Yes there are good rewards like some Key, Max Level Perks etc... but it's something that you can still obtain and upgrade by grinding.
Also, there are guaranteed endless random daily rewards (30k Munitions - it's the currency that you normally earn by playing - or a random boost, or 30 Golds, or an Epic Card Pack) that you claim just by logging into the game.
I can't say the game is brutally Pay-to-Win even if could be frustrating for lowbies.
However, i find pretty fun upgrading my base and units so i keep playing, but i'll support them just if i'll see a progress in the future, a progress in terms of contents (more traps, units, buildings, features like better PvP or co-op, less bugs, etc...), and less abuse of Golds.
Besides PvP and Alliance Battles, there is the endless mode against AI, with leaderboard of course.
Well, the game is free and pretty fun. Just take a look.

Legend of Grimrock 2 is an old school first person non-linear dungeon crawling role playing game. Improves on the first game in every way. Incredibly challenging. Lets us go outside!
Read the full, and lengthy, review below!
Legend of Grimrock 2 is an old school grid-based dungeon crawling role playing game wherein players take control of a party of four prisoners that survive a shipwreck and wash up on the mysterious Isle of Nex. They soon find out, however, that they are not alone and to make it off the island alive they have to overcome the challenges devised by the ominous mastermind of the island.
After playing around 10 hours
of Legend of Grimrock 2 I can tell you without the shadow of a doubt that the game has managed to take everything that I loved from the first Legend of Grimrock and somehow make it better. Almost Human Games have given us extra flexibility and variety when creating and setting up our party with new races, classes, abilities and perks, an expansive and open world to explore and survive in with a full day and night cycle, new multi-tiered zones ranging from tropical shorelines to rat-infested mines, lush jungles, to creepy graveyards, overgrown ruins to long forgotten tombs, ancient temples to poisonous swamps and then the freedom to move between them all at will and with ease. The game's engine handles the great outdoors wonderfully, too, and it all looks much better than I thought possible for a game of this type. There are now more secrets, puzzles, riddles and items than ever before and then, most importantly, the same great, addictive and thoroughly challenging old school style of gameplay and combat. Progression through the main plot of the game is done in a non-linear fashion that rewards players that take their time, explore and immerse themselves fully.
Grimrock 2 also features a built-in Dungeon Editor that seems a lot of fun. I've only briefly tested it but in the 15 minutes I spent using it I was able to create an actual dungeon I could walk around in. I plan on sinking some time into making my own content for the game once I've completed it.
All of that said and after playing an unhealthy amount of the game over the past couple of days I can say with much surity that
This game will appeal to long-time fans of the series, and now almost extinct genre, and newcomers alike. Although, it must be said, both of the aforementioned groups will still find themselves struggling with some of the enemies, challenges, puzzles and riddles presented to them during their time on the Isle of Nex.
Check my likes and dislikes below!
Legend of Grimrock 2 was developed and published by Almost Human Games and is the sequel to 2012's Legend of Grimrock. If you don't own and haven't played the original yet I recommend buying the Legend of Grimrock Bundle and playing the first game before the second, it is also a great experience and will let help you hit the ground running in Legend of Grimrock 2.
Here's my quick(ish) list of Grimrock 2 likes and dislikes. I didn't include everything in here, but hey, should still be enough to get you informed.
I'll continue to update the likes and dislike section as I play through the game and learn more about it. Thanks for reading and rating, I hope you all have as much fun as I am playing Legend of Grimrock 2!

Always-online singleplayer game with decent handling and car customization, and annoying rubberbanding. Ridiculously heavy policecars, with rubberbanding. Microtransactions that aren't necessary. Inaccurate representation of racetracks (elevation at least). Otherwise good map.
Let me get one thing straight, this game isn't a proper MMO. There'll probably be 1-4 players visible at a time, while sometimes it goes up to 8, and sometimes it stays at 0. The car count in races is up to 8 in both singleplayer and multiplayer PvP or Faction-v-Faction.
It's basically an always-online singleplayer game with random people in it occasionally.
Multiplayer races give ~16k each and take a few minutes.
If you want a multiplayer lobby quickly, go to one of the first regions (Midwest or East coast) as there are the most players there. Also go for Free-for-All, Faction-v-Faction lobbies take longer, but if you desperately need a FvF lobby join one of the first factions (Wolves or Eagles) as they have the most players.
Speaking of factions, if you want to raise your faction rank and get a bigger daily salary you want to play the PvP lobbies in your faction's region, do the faction missions in previously mentioned region, or send your (Uplay) friends to do those faction missions, which vary in length between a few minutes and a few hours. Don't worry, your friends won't have to actually complete the missions for you, they won't even know you sent them! It's just a three hour timer, after which it randomizes if the mission was completed based on a percentage value shown to you before you send them. If the mission was completed, you get a quarter of the normal payout (max. ~16800B). You can send multiple friends to the same mission at once (after getting a perk for that) and increase the odds of completing it, easily hitting 100%.
Speaking of perks, you can only fully complete the perk list by paying more real money. Normally (no preorder) you can max out all the car performance perks, or some of the discount ones (up to 30% off cars and parts). If you preordered and got 100CC (in the first half of the story) spend them on buying more perk points. They're (right now) the only thing you can't buy using ingame cash (B(ucks)). Using those 100CC (Crew Credits) you can max out both the car performance perks and the discount perks.
The max amount of people in a crew is 4. Those other 3 will be able to come with you in most story missions and all of the faction missions.

The car handling, from my experience using an XBOX 360 wired controller and an older steering wheel (240 degree, with FFB, sequential shifter and paddles) on hardcore assist settings, is good. I can't explain things like this very well, but it's balanced towards simlike. Much better using the wheel, but the XBOX controller is fine too. Even using a keyboard it's perfectly drivable.
There is a literal metric f*ckton of rubberbanding that's annoying in races, but even more annoying in the takedown and getting chased missions. It's also active in all police chases, so don't be surprised (just frustrated) when you see a Crown Vic doing 300 km/h.
The policecars also weigh a [quote from start of the line 3 lines up], so don't expect to be pushing them much. Instead, expect to have your car do an endo when they stop in front of you and expect to be spun out a lot.
Customisation is decent, in all specs you can change car color (Metallic/Anodized/Iridescent), reg. plate type (unlockable), Interior color (usually 3 different color areas), and rims (standard/road/racing/offroad/classic/special)(silver/black/gold/white usually, no matte). Raid and Circuit specs have no other customisation. Street, Dirt, and Perf on the other hand usually also have bumpers (front/rear separate, ~8 different), sideskirts (~2), spoilers (~2), and hoods (~5).
Car price is defined by "coolness level", separate for each dealer.
Performance parts are gained by completing missions, or more commonly, skills. Skills are short challenges scattered across the map, are triggered by driving through them, and can be disabled in the options. When you become lv.50 (max) you'll unlock platinum ranks for skills and missions. Then, if you get the platinum rank in any level event, it'll roll a lv.40-50 platinum part for your current car. This part can later be bought in the tuners for cars in the same spec for about 30000B. Jumps take the shortest time and are the easiest, so they're best to grind on. Raid cars are a lot harder to grind using jumps than any other spec.
The map has lots of variation and it takes some 40 minutes to drive across it using roads. You truly can go everywhere you see, except things like Canada, Mexico, over the ocean, some peoples' yards, and most docks/piers.
The mirrors work in 3rd person but not in 1st person. The story isn't particularly interesting, doesn't give you much money at all, and isn't particularly long either. Microtransactions are only needed if you want all perks at the same time, perk points can be taken back and reapplied to different perks without loss. Keys are fully rebindable on all control devices (except maybe things like ESC). Racetracks are flattened. There is manual, even with clutch. Noone chats. These are miscellaneous things I wanted to say.

Legend of Grimrock 2 is a game that truly deserves the ‘2’ behind the title. It’s bigger and better than Grimrock 1 in every regard while staying true to the  feel and gameplay concept of its predecessor.
Not surprisingly Grimrock 2 is still a dungeon crawler in the spirit of games like Dungeon Master or Eye of the Beholder. You move your party of four characters through the gameworld using a grid based movement system,  solve puzzles and kill monsters in real-time combat along the way.
So what did change since Grimrock 1? Quite a lot.
Instead of a single, linear dungeon you now have a semi-open world with beautiful outdoor locations and lots of different dungeons to explore. And you can explore them in almost any order, so if you get stuck on a puzzle you don’t have to check out a walkthrough guide to proceed, instead you can go somewhere else and come back later with new ideas or hints in your backpack. One other advantage of it is the games' increased replayability – in Grimrock 1 you maybe missed a few secret areas while fighting your way through the dungeon, in Grimrock 2 you can finish the game without ever seeing a good part of the gameworld.
Combat is much more challenging now, enemies move and react faster. Their AI was improved as well so many of the cheap tactics that you could use in Grimrock 1 don’t work anymore.  Single, slow monsters can still be defeated quite easily using the ‘strafe and run’ tactic, but there are more than enough challenging fights with multiple and/or fast enemies.
The UI and some of the gameplay mechanics were overhauled as well. The skill system is more versatile and makes more sense now, alchemy is more useful as there is a larger variety of more powerful and interesting potions available, there are new weapon types like firearms and many other detail changes.
And of course there is much more content – the game is easily twice as long as the first game, there are more different dungeon types, beautifully crafted outdoor locations,  more different weapons, more different enemies, more puzzles, more everything.
If you are interested at all in the genre this is a must-buy. It doesn’t get any better than this…until Legend of Grimrock 3 comes out.

All this must be done whilst searching for 11 tapes scattered around a set of random repeating areas with enemies to get in your way. Keep in mind, one hit from an enemy and you're dead and start from scratch. However, enemies react differently to being shot in different places, for example: shoot one in it's weapon and it won't be able to hurt you, just annoy the hell out of you.
Cleverly built, addictive little game that gives you a real rush when you master it.

VVVVVV is a retro styled 2D platformer by Terry Cavanagh, creator of dozens of free games. You play as the fearless leader of a team of dimension exploring scientists who inadvertently crash, and are separated. The game involves exploring the strange world you've found yourself in, and reuniting your friends.
VVVVVV explores one simple game mechanic: you cannot jump - instead, you reverse your own gravity at the press of a button. The game focuses on playing with this mechanic in a variety of interesting ways.
The game is designed not to artificially gate your progress. In VVVVVV there are no locks, no power-ups, no switches, nothing to stop you progressing except the challenges themselves.

I bought this game on sale, so it wasnt such a great cost for this game and that did help in itself. I would be frustrated though if i had bought it at the original price. So therefore i cannot recommend it unless its on sale.
I have to be fair though, the developers seemed to have put a lot of love into this game and it really feels great to play. I liked the different levels, the story (at least at the beginning of the gameplay before it got confusing), scarring for resources was also a challange and the graphics really appealed to me. A big plus would be for the backgrounds wich in some parts are astonishing.
So sum it all up. It was a smooth, fun and interesting playthrough but it left me wanting for more gameplay and more answers. I am intruiged at getting the expansion for it, so its not a bad game. Just a bit to short, to confusing at the end and to expensive at the original price wich is why i cannot recommend it without a sale. But if its on sale and you want a fun ride, pick it up and hop on the train, to The Final Station.

I didn't like my experience with 10 Second Ninja X, just being honest and sitting through it it does have some problems.
First of which I think is the over use of death objects to acheive a unrealistically high difficulty without any creative level design.
Secondly I think movement is a bit quirky especially vertically which is slow in a game all about going fast, and sometimes messes with expectations of location when using a shuriken, sometimes messing up a otherwise perfect run.
Another was more of a annoyance, vareity this game sorely lacks it.  Literally all objects are instant death and theres only two off the top of my head ways to die, electricution and crushing.  Compare that to super mario brothers, on the NES where you can fall into bottomless holes, get hit by enemies, burned by pirahna plants, eaten, etc.  All im saying is that though the game itself has 6 differently themed backdrops, they're nothing but backdrops.
Something else I have a problem with is the forced story and the odd places it goes for an indie game.  First off there's a small break every time you finish a set of stages, this im okay with for a small break of monotiny.  But what it does after that, purposefully annoy the player with a worthless character, and its not like you hate the guy, hes a minor inconvinience, get past him and done, do the stage.  But its what happens later, you know expecting it to go AGAIN with this boring sequence where he dies yada yada.  And then you know what happens?  GUY COMMITS SUICIDE.  THIS GAME HAS A CHARACTER THAT COMMITS SUICIDE, LIKE WTF?  Everything else is happy go lucky any channel would play this for a younger audience, and you threw it out with that one scene.  HONESTLY WHO APPROVED THAT?  You honestly might have lost major word of mouth because of that.
And finally its the oddly surgent difficulty, as I mentioned earlier this game has a problem with overuse of death objects.  This is mostly present in the first set of stages, then it gets WAY EASIER.  Honeslty I expected a challenging game and then I got bored just playing on to see that challenge I once even didnt even have to complete the last two stages of a set because I was perfect on the last few before them.  And then the last stages return to the difficulty level of the first except they seem really well designed in comparison.  If they had more of that earlier in with a little bit of filler maybe I would have liked this game a lot more.  But instead they had to be the new super meat boy and have just have electric death everywhere.  Honestly why doesnt the ninja just wear a rubber suit?  Its not the most comfortable thing ever BUT HEY YOU DONT DIE TO THE THING THATS EVERYWHERE.  Its like being a fish without guills you go under water for a bit come up to the surface for a long time and then dip your head into the water to see how things have changed.
Graphically Im not too bad on the graphics, some of the earlier stages are definately dull looking.  And the music is okay if not lacking in vareity, if im in a casino level I'd assume there'd be a change to a more casino vibe then the stuff that's been playing since the start of the game.
I personally think that this game has nothing to differentiate itself enough from the crowd, especially from the last game to justify a purchace, unless you're a masochist, and then you should just skip the middle bits so you dont sleep on the job, and enjoy the superior design of perhaps the last games levels?  Yeah those levels I feel have a better design and now that they're revamped Its a good way to play them, even as a non fan of the original I dig the level design more than this game's over reliance on killing you over giving you a challenging level that needs mastery of a key mechanic to get a fast enough time to proceed.
TL:DR A overly typical second entry to a bland platforming game that doesn't add anything over the original core mechanics wise, or give anything a unique feel.  I feel for the pr team on this.

The gameplay is simple, and sometimes the survival aspect (keeping your train passengers alive) gets in the way of the story more than anything (you WILL miss NPC dialogue while trying to fix your train or feed/doctor your passengers), but good lord does this game have atmosphere. This game's setting, style, and to a certain extent even the story echo Half-Life 2 to a strong degree, and I LOVE it.
Pros:
-The minimalist pixel art style is actually done quite well, and creates an excellent contrast with the detailed backdrops in the cities.
-A decent length for a narrative-driven game, it ended before it overstayed its welcome
-The aesthetic is absolutely fantastic if you like slightly retro-futuristic dystopian settings
-The exploration/combat are both well done
Cons:
-Maintaining the train and keeping your passengers alive feel like busywork, and they end up making you miss NPC dialogue (which might as well be the whole reason to keep passengers alive in the first place, as the only real things to spend your money on are food for keeping passengers alive, ammo, medkits, weapon mods that I never once felt that I needed, and newspapers for more story)
Overall, this is a damn good game. It's nothing mind-blowing and it doesn't seem like it's got much replay value, but I definitely recommend it for the aesthetic alone.

I’m no expert on game design and graphics and so forth … I’m just a gamer that wants an enjoyable game that’s good value for money. No lagging, crashes and so on (you get the picture). I’ve been branded as full of crap when it comes to games so I see myself as a gamer with high expectations.
I’ve played Meridian: New World for a bit now and I found no fault in the graphics. The detail to the buildings are good. It would have been nice to be able to zoom in closer since the characters are very small (1920 x 1080). The AI seems to be functioning well on their own. The sound is pretty decent and you have dialog options. The cut scenes was lagging a bit though … nothing serious but it’s there. I’m not an online gamer so I can’t comment on that. It may not have the online capability of bigger titles but this game does not have all that security hassles either and for me that is preferable. The price is by far more reasonable than the bigger titles. You see, you do not have to pay for the attached “prestige”.
As I understand it, this game was designed by a single developer. Really? Well, if that is the case I have one thing to say to this person … you’re doing a great job. This is one purchase I will not regret. I got “bang for my buck” (pardon the pun). Do I recommend this game? I found it enjoyable so I have to say for sure! This is a flawed but enjoyable game.  That out of the way, let's briefly talk about why it was flawed.
The games combat, about half of the gameplay, is not really good until you get a weapon fully upgraded.  Even when upgraded, I stuck to two weapon: The Rifle and The Shotgun.  The reason?  Accuracy sucks on every weapon beyond the first shot tends to be wildly inaccurate.  This meant I used weapons that are real strong single shots.
Also, you die REAL easy.  At the beginning of the game you get downed in a few shots meaning every fight felt stressful and not enjoyable until I got a bunch of upgrades.
Another big issue I had was some objectives felt unclear what I was suppose to be doing until I kind of stumbled upon them.
On the upside, I loved the openworld elements.  Each district was not too large and meant they spent time making every building look and feel diffrent. Riding the motorcycle was also pretty fun to get around quickly as it feels a bit loose but not hard to control.  Also, when taking strike points they tried to make them all feel slightly different so even when doing a similar task it has something new to it that you hadn't done before.
Over all, the game was fun, the story was goofy with two dimensional characters, and I got just over 20 hours with the game.

The title says it all! Cook, Serve, Delicous! is a game that's worth your money. Do you need a stress reliever game? This can be one of them if you like to take out your stress through a fast-paced game.
I totally recommend this game to everyone. This is a very nice arcade game with upgrades for your food from one star to 3 stars. You can even buy equipments that will help your business. Experience a game where you don't just serve the food but you also prepare and cook it yourself. A unique feature of this game is that you also need to find the time to do your chores like flushing the toilet, throwing out the trash, washing the dishes, etc.
Time management is the key. Beware of rush hour, when your buzz (the chance of customers coming to your restaurant) is high, efficiency and concentration is needed. You don't want a single customer get mad at you, would you?
Pros:
+ The game is very realistic in terms of all the work present in a restaurant/food chain
+ You don't just continuously play with the same food items on your menu since there are buzz conditions where serving a food for 3 straight days will lead to a menu rot (the food is not in demand anymore) stat to the food which means if you still serve it, it'll decrease the number of customers that will come to your restaurant/food chain.
+ Addicting to the bone!
Cons:
+ It'll take a bit of practice to get used to the key bindings since it has a lot of buttons involved for every food.
Note: A new feature called the kitchen battle is still on beta where you battle other players in cooking, I guess, I haven't tried it though.

The game has potential, it's cute, but there are annoying things. If they improve it with more features, buildings, units, and make it more player friendly, it could be a much better game.
First of all, they say it's "Pay-to-Grow-Faster", so i'm playing for free and after 163 hours, i'm close to level 34 (there is a total of 200 levels). The exp boosts are not so useful, the exp is still hard, except if you are so rich to use a million of boosts.
At the end of every match there is a chance to get rewarded with Attacks Cards, with chests, or with Keys (used to open chests - you need 10-25 Keys to open chests), or with Valor Points to upgrade your units (every unit is upgradable three times), or with very rare drops like Epic Card packs (and maybe Legendary Packs, but personally i didn't find any Legendary).
Attack Cards are consumables like bombs, bonus speed for your units, bonus damage etc... that you can use during your attacks.
You can't play direct-PvP: you can attack player bases and they can't defend, but just watch your attack through a replay and choose to start a retaliation.
What's inside chests? There are different chests. Some item is guaranteed, some item is random.
Helmets (helmets give you some bonus), Valor Points, Build Points, special units etc... etc... or Hero Perks is what you could find inside chests. As i said at level 34 i didn't find Hero Perks, but i have found special units. With more luck you could find a couple of Hero Perks and a couple of special units by opening chests from level 1 to level 34, but the chests that contain them require 25 Keys, or Golds (real money), so you can't really open many chests with Keys.
I don't know if it's possible dropping Hero Perks as PvP rewards, or if the chests are the only way to find them, but i suppose it's possible as i have found an Epic Card Pack against a lowbie player, and you can receive even better rewards by beating stronger players (the rating of their strength goes from 1-Skull to 3-Skulls, and from 1-Skull Nightmare to 3-Skulls Nightmare).
So, the annoying things are the powerful Hero Perks as you require many Hero Perks for all your units... the grinding, which is very, very, very, very, VERY SLOW (it's not only negative, as it adds longevity to the game), and the Alliance Battles.
Alliance Battles is an event, like a season, where you can attack other players to earn points for your clan.
All players have three free daily Alliance Battles. When you are out of dailies, you can fight again for your alliance by paying with Golds, so you can pay with real money to buy Golds and fight more battles for your Alliance, earn more points and win the season, or you can farm by attacking players to earn points that are used to unlock more Alliance Battles (e.g.: after 100 points you unlock one more Alliance Battle - after 160 points you unlock another Alliance Battle and so on).
It's clear that's Pay-to-Win as you can buy golds and play more Alliance Battles, but the rewards at the end of the season are not essentials. Yes there are good rewards like some Key, Max Level Perks etc... but it's something that you can still obtain and upgrade by grinding.
Also, there are guaranteed endless random daily rewards (30k Munitions - it's the currency that you normally earn by playing - or a random boost, or 30 Golds, or an Epic Card Pack) that you claim just by logging into the game.
I can't say the game is brutally Pay-to-Win even if could be frustrating for lowbies.
However, i find pretty fun upgrading my base and units so i keep playing, but i'll support them just if i'll see a progress in the future, a progress in terms of contents (more traps, units, buildings, features like better PvP or co-op, less bugs, etc...), and less abuse of Golds.
Besides PvP and Alliance Battles, there is the endless mode against AI, with leaderboard of course.
Well, the game is free and pretty fun. Just take a look.
