Big Game industry is full of hype. Don't believe what you see on the trailers, I tell ya! (..at least that's true in most cases)
It's harder to know these days if the game is good or not. Many people get amped up by the hype of salesmans and their trailers with awesome music, superb graphics (which in many games  are from cutscenes and no actual gameplay) and all that stuff. Emotions sell. That has made me think a lot harder on what games to invest in.
I thought about buying this game a couple of days, during which, I watched a lot of youtube early access videos, read some reviews and so on. And finally decided to buy it. I'm now very happy I did.
Many times with big releases, there comes the feeling of money gone to waste. Not in this case. THIS GAME is, simply put, AWESOME!!
Actually I can honestly say that it's the best racing game I've ever played. I really can't compare it to the good old racing games, because it's been so long. I was a hardcore carmageddon fan back when it was the new hot stuff. Also need for speed since the first game of the series, and enjoyed them very much with maybe one or two exceptions of the NFS series later releases. I also liked Flatout 1&2 very much and Gran Turismo 5 was my the only racing game on PS3 I played a lot. And thought bugbears new Next Car Game on PC looks good, it seems to be pretty much same the formula then Flatout2, just with minor upgrades and graphics upgraded ofc - nothing this major as we see on The Crew.
I'm listing these just so that you know, what I'm rating this against, and what kind of driving games I usually enjoy.
I haven't bumbed to games like that in a looong time and was starting to worry that they're gone extinct. Luckily my fears were unjustified. The Crew really delivers!
The part I've read some critique is the phrase "never drive alone". Well, yeah, it's kinda true. There are lots of people online, but the time I've played, only one dude crewed up for a race without me asking first. But since I haven't been looking to form a crew yet, can't really complain about that.
And I must say that the time flies with this game even if you play solo races. go exploring or just enjoy driving and leveling up. Also, it probably the launch is effecting to that too because I'd think that lots of people are busy leveling up their rides and exploring. And of course, people come and go and play at different times, on different timezone and so on.
If you have 1-3 friends, who enjoy racing games and play a lot at similar times then you do, then think no further. I can't imagine how much fun this game can be if you play it with 1-3 IRL friends, with teamspeak ofc.
Another thing, the world is HUGE. Also the terrain is done very well. Mountains feel like mountains. There are lots of racing tracks, like the legendary Pike's peak, some oval tracks and one of my favorite from Gran Turismo: Mazda's Laguna Seca raceway! And many others. You can naturally also go check Death Valley, Niagara Falls, Grand Canyon and so on.
I've explored maybe 1/5 of the map in 12 hours, and I've done a lot of exploring during that time. If you think you might enjoy driving from coast to coast, it's going to take a long time to drive. Luckily there is an option to drop in at locations you've already been. Also it's possible to just take a plane and from NY to Las Vegas, and you're instantly teleported to the airport, if you don't care for joyriding cross the country.
During the 12 hours I've played so far, the negative can be pretty much summed to the following:
-Uplay.
-3-4 server disconnects during 12 hours gameplay. But if they fix this, I think it's acceptable during the early stages. The server load must be huge. But still, it's a minus because company like Ubisoft should have the resources to host the game. Better to have some extra capacity going to waste during launch, then the other way around.
-Uplay. I hate the fact that I have to run steam and Uplay at the same time
-Some very minor bugs, that really haven't effected the gameplay, for me at least. The guide thingy that shows you where the waypoint is pointing, doesn't always follow the road. This happens rarely though and only with custom map markers. I also have to note that this has happened only couple times during my gameplay, and it's a very minor thing. I hope they fix it though.
-Uplay. Steam doesn't show the people I've played with on uplay ofc, and every steam friend probably has different nickname on uplay. Makes connecting more complicated.
-The cars feel a bit rigid/stiff and slow at start, but once you get to lvl10 or so - you'll get there fast - they start to show some character. 12 hours in and I'm near lvl20 though I've done lots of exploring. I would guess that the leveling gets slower though, when you get to higher levels.
-Season pass/DLC. But this time it feels that I will be getting something for the money, unlike watch dogs for example. I of course don't like to spend 20€ for 12 cars and a bit of content, but as an OVERALL, I think this game is worth the combined price of the game + the season pass. And I can't think of another Ubisoft game I could say the same.
-Car damage could have been done better, in my opinion. I don't know if it's me, but if you crash a car to a brick wall @ 300+ km/h, something should happen (other then the cosmetic fender flying off, and then we go again). Stuff that happened in Flatout2 for example. Wheels flying. Cars being torn apart. Driver flying through the window. That kind of stuff. Or something towards that. That's how I feel about this, others might disagree since it is more towards arcade game. Still, maybe they could have implemented a toggle switch for that for those players who want more car damage.
-Cop cars sometimes way too overpowered. they will catch you with their normal cars weather you're driving on road or on corn field. Sometimes this makes very nice getaway races though, but more then half ot the time it's a bit ridiculous when you're going 280km/h and your car is like a huge magnet for cop car(s) to ram into.
CONCLUSION: 9/10 (might change this as I get more time into the game, but for now)
AFTERTHOUGHTS:
Me being on steam for years, and this being the first review I've ever written should say something of this game.
But to be absolutely clear: If you have ever liked racing games like NFS series, Flatout and racing in general and have the hardware to run this game, definitely buy this one. I was positively suprised how well my PC runs this game (a single GTX770,  Phenom II X4 940BE (3.5Ghz) cpu and 8gb RAM). And the settings are pretty high.
PS. Sorry for typos and spelling errors, english not being my native language.

So I'll start off with saying that this game was not at all what I expected. The little research I put into the game gave me the impression it was more of a Gran Tourismo/ Forza fell rather than the Need for Speed game that it is. The tuning system is very simple and easy to use. In regards to customizing performance there isn't any adjusting specific specifications. The entire system is based on "part 4" is better than "part 3" by xxx points. Simple and effective, just not what I expected.
The games racing phsyics are probably my biggest complaint. It has a very arcade feel. Say there is a pebble in the road. We'll call it 'bob'. Say you hit bob on a run with your front left tire at +100mph plus. Bob may just nudge you a little bit causing you to have to steer and correct course. Another run you may clip the same bob at 40mph on your rear right and find your vehicle 30ft in the air while spinning like you were shot from a canon. Then your next run bob decides to take your front left tire at 80mph and throw you into a spin where you may travel over 50yards off road before being able to regain control. Now I love my wrecks but some sort of consistency in the games phsyics would be expected of a game title like this.
All in all the game is still fun. It even has a ton of acheivments to unlock, plenty of vehicles for your specific taste, visual customizations are abundant also. End game gameplay is fun and they offer various styles of events to enterain your mood what ever it is.
I'll keep playing it so look for me in game. Always down for a pvp event.

Well, what can I say. After many years of feeling 'bored' with F1 games, they finaly went and hit the nail on the head with this one. Everything we asked for; formation lap, safety car, career mode, helmet customization  has all been added. But not only have they been added, they've been done correctly and not just 'thrown' in.
Here's my opinion on different parts of the game.
Career Mode:
What can I say. I was very excited and eager to start. I was first faced with Character customization, which was simple and yet efficient. Then it was the team selection, Which I'm glad you can choose any team as it makes it more 'personal' rather than being forced your Path.
R&D:
As we know it, Research & Development was kind of the weakness in the past years. But this time, it brings a whole new meaning, not only do you improve. Other teams improve and even some don't. But...
I honestly think R&D is too easy & too early. In my 1st season with Haas & into the 14th race. Toro Rosso was already 3rd Fastest, Which seemed a little unrealistic. But other than that, it's perfect.
Safety & Virtual Safety Car:
Finaly. it's back! F1 2015 felt rushed without the safety car, although the Graphics was massively improved from 2014 and some will even argue they're still the best to this day for CM. With it completely been re-done, it feels much better. Although at times, it doesn't come out when it should and it comes out when it shouldn't. In my 2 seasons I've only had 1 VSC, so other than it being rare. I can't really give feedback other than it worked great when it did happen.
But yeah that's it. The Game is great again. Thanks.

The idea of having to do every step of reloading a gun seemed great. But I had no ♥♥♥♥ing clue how to.
The game opens, its entire menu consists of a logo and a play button. So, you click on the play button and the game throws you into some random place, doesn't tell you what to do, who to kill, where to go, what to find, where you are, who you are. Nothing.
Now, I don't mind the idea of not knowing where or who you are. But the game flat-out rejects the idea of a tutorial. It expects you to know how to operate all 9+ controls for the handgun. All you do have, is a help page, when you press '?'. But this help page overlays on itself sometime. This is because I have to run the game on lowest resolution, which brings me on to my next point,
The game is poorly optimized. Really. A game with no sun (Therefore no real lighting engine) and flat 2d textures? Looking at screenshots, you'd expect this game to run on a calculator. I'm not ashamed to say that my PC is only slightly better than a calculator, but it should be able to run this in native resolution, with at least, AT LEAST, 30 fps.
But, it is an indie game... Which you shouldn't buy or sell... Cause it's still in development...

On the down side, once you reach a certain lvl nearly every base has the same gimic. The attacking AI are lemmings, and the defending AI are gods. If half the effort put into marketing skeems was applied to the AI functions, would be 1000% better game. They ignore comands, of which you have 2 options, and they are an item you must collect and choose to take with you but often given free during battle especially the one you dont need. The attacking AI is also just out for a walk, cutting the breeze, walking the dog, just happen to be carrying a gun. They aren't focused, nor in attack mode, literal lemmings, delayed reaction, idiotic targeting. Where as the defense is on high alert, ready to kill, as if aware they are in a battle, often firing from twice their range if they catch a stray bullet. Rewards don't scale. So that wow 5K boosted from easy fight at the begining is really great. But when everything costs over 100k to upgrade and that is the only fight you can win, with out paying money. The grind is real, and gets old fast. And I think they were decreased, and for that get ♥♥♥♥ed. 2K per fight, 8K reward unboosted for triple red skull wtf are you thinking. In similar games you attack to get resources. Makes sense right, you go out and claim victory and bring home the reward. In this game you defend, to gain resources faster, and honestly there are points where it is more fun. Prior to droping some cash especially. It should be the complete opposite. Attacking should be more fun and more rewarding. The attack cards should be just that, stikes and benefeits. The comand cards should be internal/permanent. Rally flag on 30 sec cooldown and focus fire on 1 min cd. To have some control of the bumbling idiots that scurry towards the traps and mazes of an AI enemy who is focused and ready to kill. Also each unit should be given formation preference, just like the veteran option in the HQ. Except back, mid, front. Never should not 1, not 2, but 3 medics run out into sniper tower in front of 3 riot gear troops shielding them. 1 because they are healers, they should know they are healers and have some focus on that how ever little, I mean, its their job right, not just a passive thing that happens. And 2 because the medics range is 24 and the riots is 16, so if the ♥♥♥♥ing riot is engaged why the ♥♥♥♥ would the medic not fire from behind him at what ever he has targeted, and why run out in front to fire. Defense seems to have some kind of attack priority, at least in my experience. Always seem to get high threat target or medic down first. Where as attacking troops will do the same thing over and over, even if they just saw 20 other troops do it and die. Or they will target a unit instead of the 1% health building over and over while the unit solo wave after wave of them with the buildings help. Which would be a second option to add to troops along with formation preference, attack preference, unit or building perhaps. I am not a programmer, I know the game is still under developement, although its been out on PS for a while I guess. Dont know how some are lvl 200 already with such dismal rewards, or why there is even a lvl 200. Most bases are indestructable by lvl 25. I think these would be simple things to add, and its an idea to fix current state. I think it would make it way more fun and balanced. Maybe people could start attacking the 6 7 8k or higher bases people have if they had a little more control over troops. I mean regular players not the cashers. I dont get it, my generation, we bought a game and played it. Not got a game and paid it. If you make the game fun people will wanna buy into it, or want more stuff. But these games today you have to pay for more turns, or pay for more colors. I get it, the cosmetic marketing, but some games are so bad for it. Cooking is done by selecting the customer (1-9) and following through with the preset key-presses needed to cook the meal they requested ('k' for 'ketchup' etc) within the allocated time-slot; the more orders you complete perfectly, the greater your 'buzz' value, which, in turn, brings in more customers. While this system works pretty well, on recipes with a large number of potential ingredients you can end up encountering difficulties - Cabbage, Celery and Cinnamon can't ALL be bound to the letter 'C', so you can end up having some unintuitive combinations.
Beyond the time-management and, essentially, typing-speed - the only other depth to the game is in the money resource-management - which can be spent on either more recipes (each with their own pros/cons based on times-of-day and clientelle) and equipment (which gives passive bonuses - eg. need to do non-earning chores [such as cleaning the loo] as often).
My biggest complaint about this game is that it feels artificially long - it takes 20 days to earn your next 'star', even if all the other criteria has been met - making it sometimes feel like a bit of a grind if the unlocks you're earning each day are not for the recipes you're hoping for.  That said, the game does a good job of feeding you rewards often enough to keep you playing, and those days that you manage to get a perfect score do feel like a real achievement.
This is not the 'war and peace' or 'charles dickens' of gaming - it's a fun throwaway game that is more fun than you're probably expecting it to be.  Definitely recommended - particularly if
ticked some of your boxes.

It's hard for me to de-recommend this game, because it's not -bad-, I just think it is a bad idea.
Amazing World is clearly aimed at children, and for what it is, I think it's excellent work, but is this really how anybody wants their child spending their time?
It's a very happy, positive, friendly game with charming artwork and simple controls. Frankly, I think Ganz has done splendid work with this, in terms of design and production, but I just can't get over it being an MMO designed for CHILDREN. As in little children. I'm not against games being designed for children if they are educational, or in some way productive, but I didn't encounter anything I could describe as educational while I was in the game. In that way, I can't see any good cause for this game.
The game encourages you to help others by rewarding you for doing various chores and solving puzzles. I guess you could say this is teaching good social behavior and work ethic, but real life is not like that at all. In reality, you spend a century or so working yourself to your grave and get nothing out of it. I am not a parent, though if I were, I would hardly stand for my child being (brainwashed?) made to think that doing good things means getting good rewards. Rather they should learn about the real world and be prepaired for what to expect from it. So in that way, I think this game is probably even harmful.
I suppose there may be some small audience this game is just right for- if you have a small child that is handicapped in some way that prevents them from playing or studying and they need some nice way to pass their time between surgeries or treatments or just in general, then perhaps this could be a good escape for that child to do something entertaining that isn't full of distasteful nonsense like guns and explosions and zombies. Outside of that, I think any child is better off doing something that builds real skills like drawing or playing with building blocks.

The monsters in the game provide nothing new in the way of gameplay innovation. The three enemies can be defeated by, in order:
- wait in the closet until the enemy goes by
- walk, don't run, next to the enemy
- walk/run away from that enemy until they disappear
Spoilers: it indeed is all a dream! Sure, there's a bit of extra story there, but if the idea of playing a character through a nightmare landscape with no consequences doesn't appeal to you, you probably won't like this game either.

Do you like just going crazy and doing whatever you want in a free-roaming game like Grand Theft Auto and Saint's Row?  Well Just Cause 2 not only lets you do that to your hearts content but it's the core of the story and the gameplay.  You get thrown into an insanely huge country where sadly the buildings aren't on fire and all the vehicles are in perfect working order.  You are sent to rectify this mistake because God actually wanted everyting to be blown up free the people from their oppressive president... and you are God.  Lots of missions, upgrades, collectables, and secrets galore!  If you are a completionist like me and can't stand anything less than 100% then you are in heaven because there are over 250 different areas to explore, grab all the stuff, and then subsequently destroy.
It's a great game in that it doesn't take itself too seriously.  They know what you are going to do with this world and they don't take up too much of your time with story and let you get to it.  There is an element of America is the best country ever blah blah blah patriotic circle jerking blah blah blah but it's easily forgotten when you launch a Ferrari off a bridge, jump out of it, cling to a helicopter, hijack it, reduce an oil refinery to fiery ashes, jump out of the helicopter, and steal another Ferrari.  And did I mention you can essentially fly?  Yeah, it's like Grand Theft Auto with superpowers.  Enjoy.

I was surprised at some of the car choices they had available, and then some of the cars they left out, but overall, this is truely a petrol head's MMO. I suspect they will be releasing DLC for more cars, considering they left out anything from Hennesy, Ferrari, Maserati, Bugatti and some legendary classics such as the Lambo Contach and Diablo.
The late and great Mr. Shelby is represented well as his last creation is probably one of the meanest cars available for it's specialization.
There's is a little something for every type of racer, Rally(Dirt), Street, Circuit(Traditional Races), Baja(Raid), then your borderline street legals (Perf). And all customizable according to the cars specs.
Cars range from the 67 Mustangs, 69 Camaros and 70's Chargers to your top end cars like Pagani, Lamborghini, Luxury Sports such as the Mercedes SLS AMGs and BMW M series even the Bentley S along with a little everything in between.
The driving simulation leaves a little to be desired, but with so much to do in the game you will barely notice it.
The Downfall to this game... Ford Explorers. They are everywhere and ready to screw you over on the turns that matter, the skills that you need gold or plat completion on for that car part you need, or in general they're just brake checking you while you're going 300 miles in your Dodge Viper SRT 10 fit for circuit racing and when you adjust to avoid, they'll be sure to change lanes into oncomming traffic so you rear end them. Also, the game unnaturally pulls you from your direction of travel at times and you need to compensate for that, which can mean over compensation and ruining your run. Public enemy #1 is still those damn Explorers.
Overall 9/10

Pretty fun game in terms of mechanics and whatnot, albiet rather short. Nothing special though. The only reason I play pixel-graphics 2D sidescrollers is for the story.
But man oh man was the story disappointing.
There's a difference between "leaving the story open to interpretation" and "we're  lazy and can't be bothered making a real  storyline, so we're going to leave our game half-finished and slap on a lousy ending while passing it off as a twist ending"
Somebody call MatPat, we've got a new FNaF! (I have nothing against FNaF, but it is notorious for having more content story-wise in Game Theory videos than the actual game itself).
Honestly, a Jacob Sartorius fanfiction would probably have a more coherent plot than this game.
And before you say it, no, it is not a matter of whether or not I "understand" the story - there's nothing to understand. There are no explanations, just little ambigious statements that seem to be leading up to some big climax, some huge reveal, only to end abruptly. And there are no alternate endings.
Here's a great analogy: Imagine a movie studio getting a bunch of teaser trailors for different sci-fi movies with similar themes. The studio then proceeds to paste all of said teaser trailors together into a feature-length film. That's what this game is like. One, big, four-hour long teaser trailor.
Ignore all the story, pretend it's just another zombie apocalypse game, and you'll probably have fun.

This game delivers what it promises. It's a Huge open world to explore, the customization is very diverse, though, lacking from car to car (This Raid Spec Car drives just like this Raid Spec Car I wanted to replace, which fells like a horrible Dirt Spec car, ETC…), and the multiplayer is questionable, but playable.
The open world is just that. An open world. Literally, if you start in New York with your fastest, corner carving monster at the end of the game and drive West, you might hit water in 30 minutes if you haul serious♥♥♥♥♥ Enough said about that…
Customization is great, until you hit Raid Spec and, to a lesser extent, Circuit Spec. No Body modifications, which though it is not a horrible feature, it does take a little away from the game when you get into Multiplayer, and everyone's car looks exactly the same… And the Raid Spec is, by far, the worse handling rendition I have ever seen. If there was not a Dirt Spec, it wouldn't be that bad, but when my R34 Skyline (With a ride Height of about, say 4-5 inches) can take a good 8 foot jump without breaking a sweat at 140 MPH, yet a Silverado looking like a Baja competitor (With a ride Height of 1-1.5 FT) takes the same jump around 100 MPH and spins, contorts, rolls, and loses an insane amount of speed is not balanced in the right way.
Another bit of Customization that I like and dislike is that the car (Or truck) that you start with makes little to know difference. In fact, the best Performance Spec car is a Ford Focus, if you take the time to grind and get maximum level parts with the best bonuses. You take an Aventador against the Focus, and in Full Stock Spec, the Lamborghini wins, hands down. But as soon as you drop the Aventador into a "Specialty", it drives as if it is running on 4 cylinders with 3 of its tires slashed…
The Multiplayer is worthy of Next Car Game: Wreckfest… All of my experience with the Random Lobbies have been people driving SUV's either careening all over the road, or driving the wrong way just for the sake of making people rage. Bear in mind what was said in the previous paragraph… It doesn't matter if they're in a Silverado and you're in an Aventador: They are both potentially equal.
… That's my opinion. Not saying you should buy it or pass on it, but hopefully this review gave you a little insight into what to expect should you buy it.

If you are reading this and you are like me and have been sadly very disappointed by the recent F1 games here is what you need to know.
9/10 - Season & Career single player modes are both in-depth & immersive.
7/10 - AI has been greatly improved, It's still not human but it's the closest it has ever been. (keep an eye out for AI in the wet, they drive like they are in the dry)
8/10 - Visually the game is stunning even at 4K or 21:9 & wider. (still clearly bound by console fidelity)
9/10 - Engine Sound, yes its the turbo era, But Codemasters have nailed the sound even down the finest of engine/turbo details. They really did some work here.
8/10 - Atmosphere sound is rich and immersive with great menu music & some of the best commentary the franchise has ever featured. (Sadly no Martin Brundle or Ted Kravitz)
8/10 - Racing Wheel & Pedal FFB & feeling is great. It's not Assetto Corsa but even a finely tuned Fanatec wheel owner can still enjoy some of the detailed rear wheel slip or kerb feeling.
7/10 - Car Handling and Physics are improved. Again this isn't Assetto Corsa or iRacing level. Dry racing is still on rails, wet weather feel has seen some improvements and feel more challenging & rewarding when perfected.
8/10 - Track design has finally been updated to better represent the real life counter-parts. Some tracks had previously not seen layout updates they where first implemented in F1 2010. Melbourne T10 to T11 no longer has grass against the wall. FINALLY!!!!!!
9/10 - Voice Command, This feature seems trivial. But it simply works, see the list of valid commands below and make sure you speak with a clear tone of voice into your mic. "Leave Me Alone" & "Shut Up Jeff" are genuinely valid responses just FYI. LOL!!!
Overall this franchise has finally seen some love & revitalization it badly needed. While I understand the difficulties of a yearly cycle, this looks like a game they spent 2 years making not 12 months.

Absolutly amazing. This game is the perfect in-between of GT and Forza. People have been compairing this game to Forza, but in reality they shouldnt because its totally different. Other racing games have been about one thing; race, win, upgrade, and repeat. But this game adds character that everyone has been craving in a racing game. The social racing style gamepaly is incredible to say the least. Example: I pulled up to another driver and reved my engine a little and we both did a burnout and drag raced to the end of the Vegas Strip. Afterwards I flashed my lights and he flashed back and we took off. Do I know that person? Will I ever see him again? No and probably not. But it was insanly fun none the less. Now on to the pros and cons because there are actually quite a lot of both.
Pros:
1. The open world (probably the games best feature to be honest) is to say the least HUGE. But is also deatailed very very well.
2. The Customization is also very detailed and expansive.
3. Social Interactions and ease of joining friends. Very very easy to join friends.
4. Very little to no delay or lag. When playing with friends its not like TDU2 where you see someone teleporting next to you (Ah the memories). Its to say the least almost seamless even at high speeds.
5. The little need to spend real money on crew credits. I made enough in one day to buy the La Ferrari. Its easy but no OP easy.
6. The graphics on the cars and people. I would give the graphics on the cars a 9/10 for the exterior, and a 8.6/10 for the interior. The people on the other hand are easily 10/10.
Cons:
1. The relativly small number of cars in the game is quite frankly annoying. When you compare to other games its very small. My view on this will probably change with the DLC coming out next month.
2. Missing specs: now this is really really annoying to me. Not because there are missing specs. Its that you can still race against those specs in races. If your going to pull specs then pull them completely. Not just from players.
3. Level cap of 50. I got to 50 in 3 days. If its that easy you should have a level cap of 150. That would take a lot longer.
4. You can't sell cars. Now come on Ivory Tower, I know theres some old TDU devs in there.
5. Barley any cosmetic tuning on the raid and circuit specs. You cant tune any of the body work besides wheels and color on those 2 specs. I can understand the circuit spec (not wanting to misrepresent car companies), but raid?
6. Broken car level system with AI. The rubberbanding (When they slow down when your behind and instantly catch up when your ahead) in insane when doing non story AI races. Wheres the logic when a level 800 circuit spec can catch a level 1128 circuit spec easily?
To top this review off even with those cons, this game is still absolutly stunning. If I could go back and preorder it over again, I would do it in a heartbeat. The last time I had this much fun in an open world game was probably skyrim. Its amazing where your on the top of a mountian or in a city and see something far in the distance and you can say "I can drive there". Good job Ivory Tower and good job Ubisoft.
My final score for this game is 9.7 out of 10.

Receiver, in my opinion, is quite an underrated game.
I am, unfortunately, a gun nut, so maybe this game is a bit more enjoyable for me. But this game is underrated imo.
When you get put into the game, you'll start off with one of three possible handguns. The Glock, 1911 or a revolver. Initially, you'll realise the controls are a bit hard to get used to. Several different controls for different functions, such as pulling the slide back or checking the chamber.
In an hour or two's time, you'll find that you will barely need the help (which you can get by pressing '?', advanced help is holding '?') anymore. You'll also find yourself carefully treading through the map, taking out each bot that you come across quite easily, until one of those damned flying bots get you.
There is also a backstory to this game; you pick up tapes and you listen to tips and stories behind the bots and what is real and what isn't. Then, there is also the thing about ammo. I have seen several reviews complaining about ammo; except I never found myself, not even once, in a situation where I have no ammo and am surrounded by enemies. There are many bullets lying about; you just have to look really carefully in corners and under, on top or inside objects. You'll also find yourself properly conserving ammo and knowing which part of the bots to shoot in order to deactivate them.
Unfortunately, you die if you get hit even once by anything at all.
The realism this game brings is quite astounding, and eventually I became a gunslinger against bots. On record it shows 1.9 hours, but I played more than that. My computer had a meltdown while I was playing it (because I have a not-so-good laptop) and the game accounted to me only 9 minutes of playtime, which, of course, is incorrect.
This game is pretty good in general, however, the price is a little bit high. I got it for free on Humble Bundle (also the way I found out about the game). Might not be worth your time if you are into fast-paced action shooting games like Call of Duty.

Well first things first...the game is gorgeous and graphically slightly better than 2K15...After almost 10 hours of continous play, no random crashes or FPS drops and no start up problems (although it may take a while for the game to open from the Stone Cold screen). The game is quite well optimized even for mid range PCs like mine. With an AMD FX 6300 and Radeon R7 265 overclocked edition and 8 gb of RAM, the game runs at smooth 60 FPS with all settings maxed out and 4x MSAA. With 8x MSAA the game runs at a constant 40+ FPS and around 50 FPS with VSync off.
This year there are a lot of options related to community creations and it is extremely good. One can spend hours generating content for the community.
Gameplay wise, 2K16 is much better than its predecessor. The chain wrestling and grapples are quite authentic and leads to an almost real life match momentum. However it may take some time to adapt to the new submission and kick out systems. Especially submissions are difficult to manouever but propely practiced holds can be extremey dangerous.
The Offline game mods are aplenty and offline career has a little more life than last year, where your actions and allies can shape your character's persona, much like in real life.
The Online mode is a big JOKE. Compared to online greats like GTA and CS:GO, 2K16 is a baby, with not more than 2000 worldwide players online and you will absolutely never get any opponents in any game types. You will just keep practising :-) 2K should really consider merging the XBOX and the PS community players with PC and upgrade thieir servers rigorously for delivering a good online experience to the players. As of now, the Online mode is already dead after 2 days of the game's release.
The only thing to look forward to in 2K16 is the huge roster, improved gameplay mechanics and chain wrestling systems, a plethora of offline game modes including WWE Showcase, and tons of opputunity for the community creators to keep the artist in them busy. Do not expect Online gameplay and just be happy with the offline modes and the DLCs. Atleast they gave the DLCs.
For people with random crashes and FPS drops, upgrade your GPU drivers to the latest version and also checkout some really good troubleshooting tips available online.

With Homefront: The Revolution (HF:TR), Dambuster Studios has taken on the Homefront franchise here, right it into another direction entirely: the Far Cry 3+4 style of open-world FPS gameplay. A lot of the same mistakes from the original Homefront are here: technical performance issues; & not-so-great story + character development. Though, this time around - HF:TR mostly succeeds because of its excellent graphics quality loaded with details galore everywhere + superb lighting provided by the killer CryEngine; excellent open-world; the gameplay + gunplay; & the few interesting twists + spins on the Far Cry 3+4 open-world gameplay.
Granted, this is all provided as long you can actually get around any sort of technical issues. HF:TR is certainly not without its share of technical issues, to say the very least.
Over time, from the first Free Weekend with this on Steam to even quite recently, I've had more issues than I can shake a stick at. During the Free Weekend, I had performance issues + had to limit the game's framerate via MSI Afterburner to a custom-set 35 FPS keep it stable on my PC at 1080p.
After purchasing + re-picking up the game (from where I left off, last time during its Free Weekend) just recently on the same PC (at least power-wise), more issues were introduced to me: texture flickering and/or shadow flickering. I dropped down to 1440p, to try to improve performance. I kept the graphical settings mostly at High settings. When doing so, I just couldn't see very much on the screen in certain areas for either a brief amount of time or for lots of amount of time, whether using normal V-Sync On or Off.
Trying NVidia's FastSync worked in some areas, but didn't always work out entirely in other areas. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. So, that wasn't the best solution for my flickering issues either.
Forcing a 1/2 Refresh V-Sync On to limit + sync it to 30 FPS solved those issues for me with NVidia Inspector. This is not ideal, mind you - but the game was still at least playable & not having the shadow + texture flickering here.

"The weapons are interesting here - not because of what they are (they're your typical gun types - pistols, SMG's", assault rifles, "etc), but what you can do with them. While on the fly + actually in combat, open up the Weapon Customization section (which shows your guns & what pieces you have for it) & you can quickly turn one gun into another by swapping parts out. For example, you eventually get a pistol - but it's easy enough (with a like 2 or 3 mouse clicks) to swap out enough pieces & turn it quickly right into a SMG. Since you can only have a max of 3 guns at some point, you can carry all kinds of different pieces - which is a pretty cool, different & interesting mechanic."
"Combat itself plays quite well & is just fine, as one would probably expect from a game on the CryEngine. Shootouts on the game's suggested difficulty look & feel pretty good here, which makes getting into combat a joy here. To make it even more interesting, there's two states you can wind-up in, if you get all your HP (Hit Points) destroyed."
"You can either get 'critically injured' or just flat-out 'die.' So, I'm getting 'critically injured' way more here, which sends you with all your progress right back to a nearby base + you will lose some items for surviving. The other thing that can happen is you just flat-out wind-up 'dying', instead just loads your last actual save-game instead - so, this game can be a bit challenging for me."
"You will want to also overthrow areas b/c you'll have random AI walking around in your area, who you can have following you, as you go around the game-world. This can really help to get AI tagging along with you, if you don't feel like being a Superman stuck in a spaghetti western here, just lone-wolfing & killing numerous guys in one area - since going the spaghetti western route in this game will make it much easier for you to get either critically injured or killed."
You can also sneak up on enemies & take them out, taking the stealthy approach.  This is a good approach to start down this path with, if possible, to knock down at least some numbers of opponents until you possibly get caught. Though, if you get caught + seen, you can expect for things to go down & to wind-up into your typical shootout situation. If you're doing a sneaking-only required mission that you can actually fail & have to restart from your last checkpoint - fortunately, there are only a few of these stealth-only missions.
When going through enemy areas + turning them into one of your own for the Resistance. Doing so, of course, is to your benefit. This gives you more areas you can Fast Travel between; gear-up; buy new weapons + equipment. One thing that is wonderful about this, is Enemy Areas look so different when turned from a KPA Area to a Resistance Area, making it always looks like a Revolution is actually taking place here & areas are completely being overthrown.
"While the game presents itself rather well with the presentation stuff, the story + character development is....not that good, TBH. And it's not because of the voice-acting or the dialogue - that stuff's passable & decent enough, actually. Seriously, this game does NOT give you much time to care about many characters or much depth for them, before the game finds some kind of exit strategy for them - i.e. kidnapping, death, writing them off, and/or dropping their story. And given what happens in this game with events of people getting hurt & killed brutally, you actually want to care here - but aren't given much reason to do so." There's a decent amount of Lore to find + read, also - though it's honestly nothing often truly special or spectacular here, in most instances.
Provided the player can actually get past any sort of technical nonsense + issues, performance issues; & not expect the Moon here in terms of story, character & plot-development - the gamer is in for a solid open-world FPS here. "After getting past most of the technical hurdles, the open-world Far Cry 3+4 style of gameplay in an excellent dystopian + urban-based Philly certainly made it certainly worth my while + numerous hours with it."

Neverending Nightmares is a psychological horror game from Infinitap Games. Let’s get rocking.
The Good
Firstly, two things in this game are top notch: the music and the atmosphere. Those are in order, by the way. Music edges out atmosphere for the top spot for reasons that I’ll talk more about in a second. But, seriously, the music in Neverending Nightmares is great. The menu music is creepy, the music in game is creepy, and don’t get me started on the use of bass. Spot on.
The artwork is reminiscent of an old Halloween book you might find at your parents’ place. It gives it a retro feel, but also a storybook feel with strong “You’re stuck in Hell for all eternity” overtones. A job well done.
The Bad
The atmosphere at the beginning of the game is phenomenal. Sadly, you can actually watch as the atmosphere plays as the story of the game becomes unintentionally disjointed and confusing and the gameplay itself becomes repetitive.
Whoever does the voice acting for the player character has the most annoyingly whiny voice I’ve heard in years. Every time he talks, you’ll want to beat him up and take his lunch money.
The Meh
The story, as I mentioned above, quickly becomes disjointed and damned near impossible to figure out what’s actually going on. Maybe that’s how the devs intended it to be, but I can’t understand how that’s possible.
You can “sprint” in manner of speaking. Your character starts to gasp and wheeze in less than a second. Whenever this guy wakes up, he needs to go see a doctor and get that♥♥♥♥♥♥handled.
There are multiple endings, but, the game gets so monotonous I doubt you could be bothered to play through it and see them all. One and done, I say.
Verdict: Nay
If you can get this game for next to nothing or free, sure, it’s worth a playthrough if only for how great the game starts out. If you’re planning on paying full price or anywhere near that for this game, don’t bother. There are better horror games for you to spend your money on.

DS2 is probably the worst Dark Souls game. I really disliked it but it's definitely worth playing. Recommended.
- The world doesn't feel connected, epic and unforgiving like DS1.
- DS2 IS WAY easier than DS1. And shorter. You can finish it within 15-20h if you "luck out" and don't run through too many optional bosses the first time playing it.
- Adding to the above: You get... SO... MANY... SOULS... to the point you barely care about retrieving. It's so ridiculous that you can actually lose 70000 souls and not give a f*ck. It's also a joke to get 1.5M souls within 25 hours and before reaching Nashandra/Aldia. Too many free stats (levels). Unlike DS1 where you would struggle to finish it at level 60 or so.
- About the bosses: At every encounter you realize most of them are basically the same boss simply because they all do the same thing with very little variation except for hp/dmg and maybe a buff here and there. The advantage is that you are going to kill a few of them with just 1 try, and most with 5-10, because of predictability.
- The game is way too linear. You don't have a vastly interconnected world like you do in DS1. And thanks to this you are not going to get lost as much as in DS1 but at the same time you are going to get bored more often.
- The areas are "more disconnected" but they added traveling from the start which also made the game feel shorter.
- There is... SO... MANY... MULTIPLAYER... related drops. Sigh... Probably explains why almost all the blood pools leads to visions of three buddys noobing out and dying together. Serves 'em right. Nothing wrong with this but I have a feeling the game was intentionally "dumbed down" to make it more "co-op" friendly. It's good to have a DS title for this. It's just not going to be a good DS title.
- Only Dark "Soulsish" area deserving of a "Gorgeous view ahead" comment was maybe Dragon Aerie. Also most areas are really short and followed the same recipe of visible and spreaded out itens and mobs with very few surprises. Underground areas are mostly forgettable. Small and not "epic" or "insane" at all, e.g. Compare The Gutter to Blighttown...
- Adaptability stat is a ♥♥♥♥ing joke. Why is that♥♥♥♥♥♥in the game??: Nice♥♥♥♥♥♥♥half a second invulnerability 90% of the playthrough -_- . Specially with that insane number of souls you find all the time...
- The invading AI dark spirits are just annoying. It works only when it doesn't happen so often. Like in DS1...
- I honestly don't think DS2 is a good DS game. It felt most of the time like some weird castlevania title with way more deaths unrelated to simply missing jumps.
I'm yet to play DS3 but I heard good things about it. And I know now for a fact that it can't be worse than DS2.
tl;dr: DS2 is shorter, easier and has too much wrong with it to make it a good DS game. It's still a good game though.

Neverending Nightmares may not be some ground breaking game, but it's certaintly not a bad one.
It has it's moments when it comes to the "horror" aspect. Nothing too terryfing, just lovely instances from time to time that can make your heart skip a beat.
But it's not really the kind of horror that's trying to be stressful, and make a player panic every other minute. It's strenght is more in the story, creepiness of the enviroment, overall confusion and mystery.
The art style of the game is nice. It's simplistic yet creppy, and fits the atmosphere perfectly.
There is a thing that not everyone may like and it's the gameplay itself. It is very simple.
You won't find any puzzles to solve, items to carry around, brain teasers which would seem unsolvable only to make you feel like an idiot when you finally figure them out (or look for the answer on the internet). None of that.
You also can't fight enemies, which is fine, but running away from them or avoiding them is also very easy to do.
You basically walk around all the time which may feel a little boring after a while. Thankfully levels, and the game itself, aren't too long, and the enviroment changes so it's not that big of a deal.
So if you don't mind all that, you know that hunger for answers will keep you going and you want to play a nice little horror game, then Neveredning Nightmares is a great recomendation.

I didn't really enjoy this game.  Gameplay-wise, Gone Home is paper thin.  Basically all you do is try to "use" everything available to you (imagine playing DOOM and looking for secret doors), exhaust all your options, and then once you find the right thing, a new area opens up in the house.  Then you repeat the process.  New area opens up.  Repeat process.  New area.  Then the game is done and you're supposed to feel very profound and socially progressive.
Story-wise, the game is up and down.  I am glad I went into the game not knowing anything about it, because wondering about the nature of the game is probably the only thing that kept me moving forward.  The game does a great job at leading you along the story and keeping you wondering about what you'll uncover next.  But then, halfway into the game, you realize what the game is.  You realize that there are no ghosts, no zombies, and not really even any true obstacles.  No tests of skill or wit.  The game is only a vehicle for delivering a story with a twist.  That's not really a bad thing, but it focuses so hard on getting you this story that it forgets to be a game.  It's not fun to play.  I never had an intense moment playing Gone Home.  Never had a sense of reward or accomplishment.  Just relief that I found whatever item triggers the next area to open up.  Relief that the game was that much closer to being over.  But I kept playing for some reason.
The story isn't bad.  If you're wanting a casual game that's not really a game and just a slightly interactive story, you'd maybe like Gone Home.  I personally don't understand why it was so highly praised.  Well, I kind of do.  I feel like it was mainly because, due to the theme of the story, criticizing the game might make someone seem backwards and intolerant.  But maybe I'm just cynical.

This review is strictly about FFX, because FFX-2 is♥♥♥♥♥♥anyways, but you get it free, so whatever.
This game is kind of a mixed bag. On one hand, it has this beautiful universe, with interesting and well-written characters, great gameplay and a story like I expect in a movie.
On the other hand, you have challenges like "stand in a spot and press X 200 times", "hope that no birds hit you" and "dodge the awful camera angle"
If you're looking for a game you can just pick up, get immersed in the story and complete it, then FFX is 100% for you. Pick it up, play it, love it! You don't need any strategy guide or anything. The game provides everything.
If you're lookinng for a game which you can beat 100%, all challenges mastered, you'll hate FFX so much. Many of the challenges you have to do are merely hinted at, and when you find out about them, it's often too late. Get used to frustrating moments when you have to load a save from 4 days ago, because you missed a spheroid, or whatever.
The voice acting of the english version is mediocre at best. Tidus - the main character - has awful lipsync, something I would have expected to get better in an HD remake.
The good:
+ Great Story
+ Lovable Characters
+ Good Core Gameplay
+ Interesting World you actually want to explore
The bad:
- Camera angles are fixed, and often used to "hide" secrets
- Animations are still chunky like they used to be on the PS2
- Translations are often hideously bad
The ugly:
- "Minigames" required for celestial weapons are rage-inducing and based on chance
- Many secrets are unobtainable past certain points, requiring you to reload or even start anew
- Getting 100% basically requires you to follow a walkthrough step by step or you'll screw up
Dispite all that, the game is really good and you should give it a go

Receiver is a fun little game but can I recommend it? Hard to say since I got it for free. The game is very simplistic with the main attraction being the advanced gun mechanics, which is a neat little thing that I don't think has been done in a game before. However, that is pretty much all this game is sadly. The graphics are very simple, if not even extremely simple with untextured geometry and a simple 2D backdrop. I know this game was made in about a week or so, but that does not make it immune to criticism. There are two enemies that you fight, one is a stationary machinegun turret that is rotating and the other is a mini UAV sort of thing rthat flies at you with a tazer. Both of these have weakspots such as sensors and batteries that can be shot at to disable the robot instantly. The turret in not really much of a threat, but the UAV is a big threat because it is quick, small and actually moves. But that is all there is to this game, besides the games goal to survive and collect 11 tapes to win the game.
So like I said before, the main part of Receiver is of course the guns. And they feel fun and authentic (no personal experience in real life) to operate. There are three weapons in the base game M1911, G18 and a revolver. The M1911 is the most detailed of the three with all components animated, the glock and revolver are fun to use as well but feel a slight bit unfinished sort of.
So can I recommend it? Well, not really since it quickly gets boring, but for a while it is a fun game with the unique gun mechanics that can't carry the game alone. Some kind of duel multiplayer would be fun though.

So far it's a great game. The biggest thing I don't like is that it constantly uses the internet, so if you do not have internet, or do not have a stable, constant connection, DO NOT BUY IT. Otherwise, if you have a bandwidth limit, beware when playing this game for a long period of time. This game also will send you back to the main menu if you lose your internet connection. The story in the game so far is good. I won't give any spoilers. There are plenty of cars in game, but you must earn a lot of in-game cash to be able to buy them. Car customization could be better, but this game isn't a simulation, so I didn't expect engine swaps, turbo/supercharger add-ons, etc. What's really cool is how you can modify cards for street, track, dirt, etc. One thing that bugs me is that the car sounds don't change when you switch said modification classes. For example, the Dodge Charger still sounds like the stock engine in a dirt/rally config. I did noticed when I upgraded the Skyline R34 from street to circuit version (R34 GT3), you do hear the transmission whine as you do in a race car. Kudos for that.
If you've never played this game, I should mention it is an open world like some of their other games (Far Cry, Assassin's Creed). You can drive from New York to Miami to LA, etc. Of course, it doesn't take as long as it does in real life (which is good), but it's a very neat touch Ubisoft added in for a racing game, and I hope other game makers use this as a template for street-oriented racing games.

Playing Homefront: The Revolution is like eating a five star restaurant but instead of fine china, you ate out of a crappy paper tableware; i.e: Homefront: The Revolution got nice graphics and soundtrack but it's core programming doesn't quite live up to it's triple AAA counterpart from a more seasoned studios. If poor coding and game mechanics doesn't concern you then you should stop reading here because I'm about to get into spoiler territory.
Story: It's poorly written to say the least. Basically, the story took place in a ulternative universe in which North Korea has become a super power while every other nations, including USA cower in North Korea's shadow. But the trouble is, at the same time. The game expect you to root for fictional USA like it's the real world counterpart. Which is a little hard to wrap your head around since North Korea is kind of the good guy trying to help a country on a downward spiral that is the USA to get back on it's feat but yet somehow the game expect you to root for the bum of a country that is the USA like the real world counterpart. Most of the side characters are introduce and then quickly killed off before they're established. Including, you, yes, the protagonist. Not sure how they're gonna spin a sequel out of this one if there ever will be one.
programming/game mechanics: One of my biggest issue with Homefront is that resources like medkit and consumables cost money to buy but are free at the resistance stash. Ergo, if you want to save up money to get your upgrade you'll have to avoid spending unnecessary money and resort to resupplying at a nearby resistance stash. But since the supply at every resistance stash is limited you'll constantly have to travel between them in order to fully restock your supply. IMO, the consumables should be free and endless at every resistance stash and hideout because otherwise it's just a senseless waste of time.
Secondly, some of the in game side quest involves taking picture of certain object and sometimes it's very picky about the picture you take.
Lastly, the game has rediculous amount of bug/glitches. I've upload screenshot of most notable visual bug/glitches onto steam but there are also several instances where I fell out of the map or somehow respawn outside of map and have to fast travel back inside. Which thankfully didn't cause any problem during my playthrough, but still have no excuse to be in a proper sandbox game.
TL;DR: I find Homefront's main campaign a struggle to get through, not because it's hard but because it's tedious and draining. I finished the main campaign on hardest setting but decided that I couldn't bare the game any longer than it has to be so just breeze through the 3 DLC on easy mode. Had this game come with less bugs then I probably would be fine with the price. But given the situation I wouldn't recommend this game at the full price. Maybe when it's down to 35 for the main game and 50 for the Freedom Fighter Bundle.

When people argue that videogames are not the future of storytelling, I would tell them to look here.
While I concede that shallow yet entertaining video games such as the Call of Duty franchise, or any arena-type MMORPG, do not display the emotional trials of ourselves as human beings in any sort of groundbreakingly intelligent light, they also have their merits. In my opinion there are two types of videogames in most situations: interactive storytelling and pure entertainment. While I enjoy playing games like Black Ops 2, Planetary Annihilation, Castle Crashers, and Gang Beasts, I play those knowing that I won't take anything away, besides the fun of playing with friends or solo. I don't not expect any crushingly deep emotional story or mind breaking moral dilemma. I expect fun, and those games easily meet those expectations. Then there are games like Gone Home. This game, as well as Life is Strange, the upcoming Firewatch, and the Telltale Games series are meant to be played as you would read a book. You are meant to wholeheartedly invest yourself into these characters and plotlines, to empathize and sympathize, to develop one sided relationships with the protagonists and antagonists; wishing the best for the former, and maybe death to the latter. I’m not saying you can't invest yourself into the stories of entertainment orientated games like Tomb Raider, the Last of Us, or Uncharted. Or even Black Ops. If you really relate to and care about Alex Mason, his family and his plight, I can't fault you for that. I’m just saying in my opinion that isn't truly what those games are meant for.
So, moving forward with the theme that games like Gone Home are meant to affect the player as a good novel would, emotionally, we can observe how the story of this game can be judged as such. Despite the rather snoopish feeling of going through a teenage girl's things for a few hours; if you manage to put that strange, uneasy feeling behind you, and put yourself in the shoes of the returning Katie, who has come home to an empty house and needs to investigate this oddity, the game really does come into its own. I, personally, felt all the emotions I would if my sister were to disappear. And the plot points revealed further through Sam's wonderfully voice acted journals each tore at my heartstrings, and occasionally I felt myself rushing to unlock the next entry, to reveal more of the mystery, one that is not scary or action-packed, but is still engaging and intriguing. If it was a novel, I would buy it. As a videogame, I found that the interactivity of the world; drawers, lights, drawers was well done, quite immersive. I found myself turning off lights as I left rooms (especially after finding a scolding note from the parents about the bad habit of leaving them on) and closing doors to respect the virtual privacy of the virtual non-rendered family members. And as for the secrets and simple puzzles like lock combinations and hidden areas, I felt they were fitting, without being forced.
All in all, I enjoyed this game to the very end. I played it all the way through and felt the same emotional craving for more as if my favorite book or movie had just ended, and I have to tear myself away from these beautiful characters to embrace reality again. If you like to connect to characters, to feel with them, and follow a story that you can choose to flesh out completely or leave as bare as you feel suits you; if you enjoy games that make you feel human, that make you think about and connect your life to these digital people you cannot possibly know. If you enjoy good storytelling, buy this game.
But don't expect action.
EDIT: I think the price of this game is a bit much. I wasn't aware of the pricing until recently because I got this in a humble bundle. Wait for it to go on sale. It's like paying for the hardcover version of a book when you can wait for the softcover.

While I'm recommending this game based on what's here, I have to also talk about why I WON'T be buying another WWE game from 2K until they make some changes.
First off, the game IS a bit buggy at launch and it may run, or it may not. Every single time you click "Play" it's a toss-up whether or not the game will launch. Once it launches, I'm good with 60 fps at Ultra, but whether or not the game starts up at all is the question.
Second, it absolutely ticks me off that we PC users don't get the ability to use custom music. There's no reason the restrictions of the consoles should remain for the PC version. We don't get stuck with the console graphics, but we do get stuck with the console limits on custom music. This is a DEAL BREAKER for me. I make leagues of my own CAWs, and if I can't give them custom music, that's half of the pro wrestling experience completely thrown out the window. Sure, modders will make it possible, but I shouldn't have to mod the game to get what I want out of it when it comes to something as basic and integral as entrance music.
It would be NO BIG DEAL for the game to let us point to a folder full of MP3 files, but they're simply not allowing it. That stinks, and it's the big reason why I won't be purchasing 2K17 for PC (or anything else) until I hear that Yukes/2K put the ability to assign custom music to CAWs back into the game. It's ridiculous that I would rather go back and play my league on 2K14 for Xbox 360 because it is technically inferior to 2K16 in terms of customization!
Another big problem is the submission mini-game. It just sucks, and the AI almost always has the advantage, it seems. It doesn't even make a lot of sense, and I find myself missing the old submission method. Again, 2K14 is making me happy where 2K16 does not.
If only I could get 2K14 on my PC.
What 2K16 does have is great animation, excellent graphics, and a more streamlined (though more limited) creation suite. I'm currently debating if these advances are enough to make me keep this game. Frankly, I'm still pretty ticked about the lack of custom music and I've been two seconds away from hitting the "submit" button on a refund. The only thing keeping me interested is the exceptionally nice look to this game.
But graphics aren't everything, and while the models all look great, they still don't look photorealistic, and in the end I can probably be happy with my 2K14. So I continue to debate over the value of 2K16 to me.
If you're a fan of the WWE and all the "superstars" and "divas" in their roster, then you'll probably love this game. Me? I *really* don't care about the WWE characters and would much rather play my own.
When some company makes a game like this that doesn't have any licensed characters and instead lets CAW fans make their own leagues, I'll buy two copies (if it's any good). Sadly, I think the thing that ultimately ruins this series for me is the WWE licensing, which seems to be pretty restrictive when it comes to customizing features. That's all I can conclude, anyway, because there is NO TECHNICAL REASON why WWE 2K16 wouldn't support custom music or other customizing features that are missing. So many names were removed from the announcements, so many clothing pieces, so many types of makeup, face paint, etc. and worst of all, on the PC we STILL have to go through the stupid upload process to get logos and faces into the game. WE'RE ON A PC! Why should I need to send something from my PC, to the web site, then get into the game and download it again when it WAS ON MY PC IN THE FIRST PLACE?! This is just so stupid!
Why can't I get a Fire Pro Wrestling game like this one, yet with all FPW's customization?
I suspect the glitches and bugs will be squashed and eventually the game will start up when you click "Play" instead of tossing a coin and deciding at that time whether or not you'll get to play. I doubt, however, that 2K gives a crap about patching in custom music.
GET IT TOGETHER, 2K.  This is the PC, not a console, and we want CUSTOMIZATION. You won't get another dime out of me until you wake up and support the CAW fans, too.
Consider it a thumbs up if you only want to play within the WWE using their characters or characters that fit the really strict creation content (limited names, no music, limited clothing, limited body sizing, etc), but a big thumbs down if you're a CAW fan. They really disappointed me with this one. I'm getting the refund and going back to 2K14 on my 360.
UPDATE:  Steam denied my refund request because "play time" was past 2 hours. Unfortunately, much of that time was the game "running" in the background (unbeknownst to me) after it had crashed on start-up. This IS a continuing issue with this game. Feel free to check the discussions and other tech support requests. My actual time in game was no doubt under 2 hours. My time trying to load it, trying to troubleshoot it, and dealing with technical issues was over 2 hours.  I do not think 6 hours of troubleshooting and digging into the game to see what's working and what's not working, and what's missing, is "significant playtime".
Anyway, if you're having doubt about the game, get your refund ASAP. Steam doesn't seem to care that the game process continues to run after crashing, or that the game fails to make it clear that they've completely stripped the creation suite, prior to purchase.
I feel like I got ripped off by 2K, here. Enjoy your 45 bucks, guys. I'll seriously reconsider purchasing any 2K title after this.

Banished is a wonderful little sandbox city builder/survival game. Starting with 5 families and a storage barn on Medium difficulty you work tirelessly to forge a livelihood for your fledgling community. The micro management in this game is pretty insane. Late game you can find yourself frantically rushing all over the map to make sure your citizens are always doing the right thing at the right time. The mechanics are to a great standard although some of the villager pathing can occasionally be a bit odd when they choose not to stick to roads which would increase their movement speed. There is a huge variety in jobs for your citizens to do and this allows for very expansive gameplay. Although different mapsizes are available you would find that it would take many hours of gameplay before you'd take up all the space on even a small map, let alone a medium or a large one.
If I were to compare this game to any other I would compare it to the city builder Pharoah, only more survival based. This game provides hours of enjoyable gameplay and is a nice little title to pick up, especially as it is Indie and not AAA.

I did noticed when I upgraded the Skyline R34 from street to circuit version (R34 GT3), you do hear the transmission whine as you do in a race car. Kudos for that.

You can drive from New York to Miami to LA, etc. Of course, it doesn't take as long as it does in real life (which is good), but it's a very neat touch Ubisoft added in for a racing game, and I hope other game makers use this as a template for street-oriented racing games.

I got invited into beta, i wasn't to excited at all originally when i heard about the game. Thinking "ohh yay another generic racing game of which there are hundreds already" but since i was invited to the beta i would give it a go since i haven't played racing games in a while.
To be honest i am glad i did give it a go. From the first day i played in beta i was completely addicted to the crew. It blew me out of the water and has renewed the whole racing genre for me.
The crew has so much going for it. I love the ease of quickly jumping into co-op races with others. The map is absolutely huge, i have only really explored the Mid-West and half of the East Coast (the smallest 2 states), Still leaving me with the South, Mountain States and West Cost (the largest 3).
There is a massive number of main missions which i have only scratched the surface of. There are aslo extra skills, kind of like a mini game that's completely optional from the main story quests. These skills have a wide variety to, anything from launching your car over a ramp to following race lines and many more.
The ease of use of the Tuning Specs and the fact you are able to have a street spec car, then also have the same car as a dirt spec while being able to have both cars completely different designs, colours, parts as if it was a completely separate car is awesome.

Do I recommend this game?
Yes, I had a lot of fun playing it
Would I pay full price for it?
No, wait until it's on sale. It's good and I enjoyed it, but not that much.
Note: It's an arcade style game so I've judged it accordingly. IMO a lot of people are judging the car physics and handling etc like they would for simulators, but it is an arcade game so judge it on it's merits. For an arcade style game I think it does really well.
Pros:
- Fun single player: Combined the typical "Need for Speed" storyline elements with the GTA style open world roaming allowing you to pick and choose your missions
- Co-op can be done on any missions, you can do everything on your own or with friends, you don't need to be alone for some missions or with friends for others
- Graphics are great
- Haven't encountered ANY issues with the game at all
- Hidden cars are found by exploration and unlocking areas of the map, not just winning races and earning money
Cons:
- Story Mode isn't very long, I've finished it in 18 hours and I didn't use quick travel at all so spent quite a long time driving to some missions
- Limited selection of cars, possibly because they decided to make DLC but would've been better if they were available as part of the core game
- Not many "customisation options" at all: This is for both car customisation and audio/graphics/display settings etc. There's really not that much at all compared to other PC games out there
- Limited replayability: There are some bonus missions and "skills"  and stuff for completionists to do but other than multiplayer with friends and a few longer missions, there's nothing really to do after you finish the game until more missions are released with the upcoming DLC next year, assuming you buy it
Overall, I had fun playing it and would recommend you buy it too if you've enjoyed Need for Speed/Burnout style games in the past, then you'll likely enjoy this too. I would however wait until it is cheaper before purchasing it.

The Final Station. Boy, did this take me by surprise...
The first thing you must know is that this isn't a horror game: it's just a tense ambience and very effective atmospheric game with the plot of a small story. And indeed, the small story shows when you can clear this game in just a few hours. But it is a good story nonetheless, with a very sad plot twist in the end. A very, very sad plot twist in the end.
As I said, the ambience and mood of the game are very well done. You can clearly follow the plot even though the main character never speaks on the sparse conversations and random chatter both when you're on the train or on a secure main stop. The soundtrack is... pretty decent too, actually. There are plenty of calm tracks.
Flaws? Well, it is short, no matter how you cut it. Easy enough for the average gamer with a head over its shoulders. Something I noticed is that the resolution you play it in matters a bit on some sequences; smaller resolutions tend to feel too claustrophobic when you're riding the train, impeding your clear view of what's happening on all the two cars (and potential cargo platform) as you move back and forth to keep your passengers alive. This detail in particular upset me quite a bit, as I felt I was missing something by not being able to read the passenger chatter enough. For reference, the "small" resolution I have is 1280x800, so keep that in mind.
You should buy this, I suppose, if you want a different take on what amounts to a variation of the undead horde tropes and a great emphasis on one of the best humane views on the issue. But on a discount: 15€ seems a bit much for a few hours' worth of entertainment. Your mileage may vary, of course, as it is still longer than an average movie on theatre.
Buy it. 10/10

Homefront: The Revolution is the 2016 apparent sequel (but really loosely) to Homefront. It was published by Deep Silver and developed by Dambuster Studios.
It's not a bad game, but it's far from a great game either, it's got some really big issues, for instance a lackluster story, some really bad graphics at some points (This game uses CryEngine...) and a terrible AI. But the game has some big positives as well, for instance it's gameplay is actually really fun, it pretty much plays like FarCry and that's not a bad thing, it also has some really satisfying gunplay at points, and the world is actually pretty decent as you see the effects of the revolution take over certain areas, it really gives it a lively feel. I cannot give a comment about the multiplayer as it is dead most of the time, but I will say that taking away the amazing multiplayer from the original Homefront and opting in for a mission type multiplayer was a bad option and is ultimately just not worth it.
The game is at times broken, there have been many points where I have just got stuck on an object or in an area for no reason, there was even one time where I fell through the map, now luckily the developers have been working their♥♥♥♥♥off to fix issues and comparing to what it was at release, it's pretty damn good, but not perfect yet.
The story is bad, and it's a shame because at times you can see effort being put into the game, but there have been parts where I wonder "Well where did this plot point go?" and the answer is really, it ends either too suddenly or it was resolved in a pretty mediocre ending mission, it really seems that the story was rushed as like I said, it has some of it's ok moments, but it gets broke down the next moment by an awful segment where you go survive an ambush or destroy♥♥♥♥♥♥ and seriously if you don't like the concept of 'Go here, destroy that, kill this person' then you'll hate this game as that is all it is for pretty much the whole game.
The AI is the biggest offense in the whole game, if anything I could say this AI is the worst in this type of game, i'd really put it to the point where I'd say it can be compared to Alien Colonial Marines AI, it's just broke, there was one mission where
. And really the addition of stealth is badly used, it's really not neccesary except for 1 mission, and the AI can either see you through objects or cannot see you when you're in front of them, it's actually a joke.
Luckily as said the gameplay is ♥♥♥♥ing superb, it taking the style of FarCry's gameplay was a good option and it works brilliantly here, it's so satisfying to go around claiming areas, the gunplay is amazing, getting a takedown actually feels really satisfying depending on the situation and the feel of just being able to go all over the place wrecking havoc is great.
And finally the world is mostly well done, the effects of the revolution are there, you can see you're actions taking effect over places, and it's so damn satisfying to look around areas that were once under complete KPA control to be now under revolution, it really gives this sense of success and victory, that your actions actually do something, and that surprised me because many other games don't do this well at all, but this game actually does.
TL;DR
+ Superb gameplay
+ You're actions actually make an effect
+ The Revolution!
~ Multiplayer is swapped for a co-op.... it's also dead
~ Graphics can be awful at times, this is a CryEngine game.
~ Can be buggy at times, but is mostly under control now.
- Terrible story
- Crappy AI
Overall it's a strong 6/10 game. I recommend to buy this game on sale.
